units.la: Sacrificia iterum commemorat ostendens oportere eum, qui ipsa afferat quæ qualiaq; sint habere cognita, cum animum Deus magis, quàm ipsum opus respiciat, vt in Abelis & Caini sacrificijs.
units.tr: Sacrificia he mentions again, showing that the one who brings them must know what and what kind they are, since God looks at the heart rather than at the work itself, as in the sacrifices of Abel and Cain.

units.la: Sic quod in baptismo te facturum receperis etiam atque etiam cogitatin [?] cœna Domini quid offeras cogitatin precibus mentem potius, quam verba Deo debebis offerre. Quales ergo erunt preces monachis atque nonnis intellectæ? Quin sacrificia tua quæ qualiaq; Deo offeras considera. Veluti Moses hac eorum repetita commemoratione significat.
units.tr: So think again and again about what you pledged at baptism; in the Lord's Supper think about [?] what you offer; and in prayers you ought to offer God your mind rather than mere words. What, then, will the prayers of monks and nuns be, if understood in this way? Indeed, consider what sacrifices you offer to God, and of what kind. As Moses signifies by this repeated mention of them.

units.la: Rationem docet eiusmodi, vt primum sacerdos offerat quæ debentur Domino, sua sibi feruet, offerentibus quæ sua sunt reddat: offerens autem instruat conuiuium, quo lætus fruatur cum suis.
units.tr: Rationem he teaches is of this kind: first the priest offers what is owed to the Lord, keeps his own share for himself, and gives back to those offering what is theirs; the one offering then prepares a feast, in which he may rejoice with his own people.

units.la: At conuiuia sunt quasi diuina quædam amicitiæ confirmandæ & nutriendæ symbola: Vnde & à vitæ coniunctione nomen acceperunt, & vsurpata sunt sanctis hominibus. Tristes enim qui sunt, inepti fuerint prædicandis & vehendis Dei laudibus. Verum est animum contritum Deo placere, sed quatenus reparatur ad moderata gaudia: quemadmodum dicitur, Beati qui lugent, quoniam consolationem accipient. Igitur vt lætiores animos ad Dei cultum afferrent, conuiuia peractis sacrificijs haberi voluit Dominus.
units.tr: But feasts are, as it were, certain divine tokens for strengthening and nourishing friendship; hence they have also taken their name from the fellowship of life, and holy men have used them. For sad people are unfit to proclaim and celebrate God's praises. It is true that a contrite spirit pleases God, but only insofar as it is restored to moderate joy, as it is said: Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall receive comfort. Therefore, so that they might bring more cheerful spirits to the worship of God, the Lord willed that feasts be held after the sacrifices were completed.

units.la: Et hic quidem qui nam accumbere, quibus vesci, quibus rursus abstinere debeant indicatur. Quinam accumbant, omnes inquit, filij & filiæ, serui & ancillæ, & Leuitæ quoq. Manifestum argumentum habes quàm Deus velit & ab omnibus adorari, & omnibus rursus conferre beneficia. Peccant igitur qui sese diuinis cultibus atque officijs abdicant, quasique sua nihil referat, sic ea despiciunt: veluti qui nostra ætate, si precentur sacerdotes se factos immunes autumant. Peccant itidem qui suos liberos, seruos, & omnino omnem familiam non adducunt Domino: ac neque curant religione eos imbui, neque ferunt concessô quiete sabbathi perfrui.
units.tr: Here it is also indicated who ought to recline, of what they may eat, and again from what they must abstain. Who recline,' he says, 'all sons and daughters, male and female servants, and the Levites also. You have clear proof of how much God wishes to be worshipped by all, and in turn to bestow his benefits on all. Those therefore sin who cut themselves off from divine worship and services, and despise them as if they had nothing to do with them, as those in our own age do, who claim that once they have been made priests they are exempt. Likewise they sin who do not bring their children, servants, and indeed their whole household to the Lord, and who neither take care that they are imbued with religion nor allow them to enjoy the rest of the Sabbath granted to them.

units.la: Iam quibus vesci liceat roganti, dicit, omnibus secundum benedictionem Dei largitoris. Vide quàm iniquo ferendum sit animo Christianam libertatem sub Iudæum iugum mitti. Recte sanè Paulus 1.Tim 4. & apostoli Actor.15. hos nos onere liberarunt. Ieiunauit quidè Christus, sed non quo solent illi modo: faciant si libeat periculum. Ac si peccatum sit vesci carnibus: cur illi vescuntur piscibus, quibus Paulo teste, æque sunt carnes, ac bobus atq; auibus.
units.tr: Now, to one asking what may be eaten, he says: to all, according to the blessing of God the giver. See with how much indignation it must be borne that Christian liberty is being put under the Jewish yoke. Rightly indeed Paul (1 Tim. 4) and the apostles (Acts 15) have freed us from this burden. Christ did fast, but not in the way they usually do; let them try it, if they like. And if it is a sin to eat flesh, why do they eat fish, which, by Paul's testimony, are just as much flesh as oxen and birds?

units.la: Iam quibus abstineant indicat. Primum ijs quæ debentur ac sacra sunt Domino. Vnde disce res sacras vt bona ecclesiastica, fundos, census, domos, nequaquam in priuatos prophanosq; vsus conferenda, sed reddenda Domino. Memineris aurum Tolosanum esse.
units.tr: Now he indicates what they must abstain from. First, from those things that are owed to the Lord and are holy to him. Hence learn that sacred things, such as church property, estates, revenues and houses, must by no means be turned to private and profane uses, but restored to the Lord. Remember that it is the gold of Toulouse.

units.la: Deinceps abstinendum est sanguine: Qua de re præceptum extat Gen.9. Leuit.17.19. & alibi. Causam reddit, anima carnis est in sanguine: Vnde sanguis expiationi destinatus est, qui typus esset sanguinis Christi.
units.tr: Next, one must abstain from blood. A command on this matter stands in Gen. 9, Lev. 17, 19, and elsewhere. He gives the reason: the life of the flesh is in the blood. Hence blood was set apart for atonement, being a type of the blood of Christ.

units.la: Iam sanguine vescitur qui Christi partam sanguine iustificationem & salutem in suas vires & actiones transfert: quasi suis ipse viribus cœlum petere possit & iustitiam assequi. Magna est horum hominum turba nostris temporibus. Vescuntur etiam sanguine, qui victum ex cede & rapina, & vsura sibi querunt, quia sudore pauperum partas opes ad se rapiunt. Eorum sacrificia Deus respuit apud Isaiam. In his habemus formam cultus externi qui placet Deo. Ei sit honòs in fæcula. Amen.
units.tr: He feeds on blood who transfers to his own powers and actions the justification and salvation won by Christ's blood, as if he could by his own strength seek heaven and attain righteousness. Great is the crowd of such people in our times. They also feed on blood who seek their livelihood from slaughter, plunder and usury, because they seize for themselves the wealth gained by the sweat of the poor. God rejects their sacrifices, as in Isaiah. In these people we have the form of external worship that pleases God. To him be honour for ever. Amen.

units.la: SERMO XXII.
units.tr: SERMON XXII.

units.la: 19 Cavene forte deferas Levitam cunctis diebus tuis super terram tuam.
units.tr: 19 Take heed lest perhaps you neglect the Levite all your days upon your land.

units.la: 20 Quum dilatauerit Dominus Deus tuus limitem tuum quemadmodum pollicitus est tibi, & dixeris: Comedam carnes (habet enim animus tuus desiderium e-dendi carnem) poteris pro omni desiderio animi tui carnes edere.
units.tr: 20 When the Lord your God shall enlarge your border, as he promised you, and you shall say: I will eat flesh (for your soul has a desire to eat flesh), you may eat flesh according to all the desire of your soul.

units.la: 21 Si verò procul à te fuerit locus, quem elegerit Dominus Deus tuus, vt illuc ponat nomen suum, mactabis de armentis tuis & gregibus tuis, quae dederit tibi Dominus quemadmodum præcepi tibi, & comedes in portu tuis pro omni desiderio animi tui.
units.tr: 21 But if the place which the Lord your God shall choose, that he may put his name there, be far from you, you shall kill of your herds and of your flocks, which the Lord has given you, as I have commanded you, and you shall eat in your gates according to all the desire of your soul.

units.la: 22 Et sicut caprea comeditur atq; cervus, sic comedes illa: mundus & immundus pariter vescentur illis.
units.tr: 22 Even as the roe and the hart are eaten, so you shall eat them: the clean and the unclean alike shall eat of them.

units.la: 23 Modò in hoc sis firmus, ne sanguinem edas (nam sanguis est ipsa anima) ne ergo comedas animam cum ipsa carne.
units.tr: 23 Only be steadfast in this, that you do not eat the blood (for the blood is the soul itself); you shall not eat the soul with the flesh.

units.la: 24 Non inquam comedas ipsum, sed eum in terram vt aquam effunde.
units.tr: 24 You shall not eat it, I say, but pour it out upon the earth like water.

units.la: 25 Ne comedas ipsum, vt bene tibi sit & filiis tuis post te, sed fac quod rectum est in oculis Domini.
units.tr: 25 You shall not eat it, that it may go well with you and with your children after you, but do what is right in the eyes of the Lord.

units.la: 26 Attamen sancta tua quae fuerint tibi, & vota tua tolles, & venies ad locū quem elegerit Dominus.
units.tr: 26 Yet you shall take up your holy things which you have, and your vows, and you shall come to the place which the Lord shall choose.

units.la: 27 Faciesq; holocausta tua, carnem & sanguinem super aram Domini Dei tui, sanguis verò sacrificiorum tuorum effundetur iuxta aram Domini Dei tui, & carnem ipsam comedes.
units.tr: 27 And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood, upon the altar of the Lord your God; but the blood of your sacrifices shall be poured out beside the altar of the Lord your God, and you shall eat the flesh itself.

units.la: 28 Obserua & audi omnia verba ista, quae ego præcipio tibi, vt bene tibi sit atque filiis tuis post te perpetuò: (idq; fiet) si feceris quod bonum & rectum est in oculis Domini Dei tui.
units.tr: 28 Observe and hear all these words which I command you, that it may go well with you and with your children after you for ever (and it shall be so) if you do what is good and right in the eyes of the Lord your God.

units.la: 29 Quando succiderit Dominus Deus tuus ante te gentes, ad quas tu venies, vt eas possideas, tuq; eas occupaueris, & habitaueris in terra earum.
units.tr: 29 When the Lord your God shall cut off before you the nations to which you go, that you may possess them, and you have driven them out and dwell in their land.

units.la: 30 Caue tibi ne quando (quum iam deuastatae sunt) sectando eas illaqueeris: ne scilicet requiras deos earum, dicens: Quemadmodum gentes illae deos suos coluerunt, sic ego quoq; faciam.
units.tr: 30 Take heed to yourself lest at any time (when they are already destroyed) you be ensnared by seeking them out, namely by asking after their gods, saying: As those nations served their gods, so I too will do.

units.la: 31 Nequaquam sic facies Domino Deo tuo: nam quicquid abominandum est Domino, quodq; odit, fecerunt diis suis: etenim & filios suos et filias suas igne diis suis combusserunt.
units.tr: 31 You shall in no wise do so to the Lord your God; for every abomination which is hateful to the Lord they have done to their gods; for they have even burned their sons and their daughters in the fire to their gods.

units.la: 32 Quicquid ego vobis præcipio, id obseruabitis vt faciatis, ad hoc nihil addes, ab eo nihil detrahes.
units.tr: 32 Whatever I command you, you shall take care to do; you shall add nothing to it, nor take anything away from it.

units.la: MUltæ sunt res quæ nos, si rectè reputentur, adducunt, vt simplicem illam, & ab ipso Deo præscriptam religionis formam posthabitis reliquis omnibus retineamus: quas Moses, vt quæ peterent Israelitæ etiam vellent, enumerauit. Sed quoniam velle satis non est, ni detur etiam posse, Moses uti voluntatem viribus adiuuaret, rationes iam commemorat quibus queat hæc simplex forma retineri.
units.tr: Many are the considerations which, if they are rightly weighed, lead us to hold fast to that simple form of religion prescribed by God himself, setting aside all the rest; and these Moses set out, so that the Israelites might also will what they seek. But since willing is not enough unless the power is also given, Moses, to help the will with strength, now recounts the reasons by which this simple form can be preserved.

units.la: Earum prima est, uti Levitas foueant, hoc est ministros religionis, quippe qui sint eius custodes, in hoc constituti, vt ne quid patiatur decedere. Altera est, vt intra limites eorum rituum, quos & Deus præscripsit, & ministri illi custodiunt, ipsi se contineant: nec suas ad e-uagandum propensæ naturæ frena laxent. Tertia est, vt verbum Dei purum putum, ac neq; malis exemplis neq; expositione sinistra flexum retineant.
units.tr: The first of these is that they should cherish the Levites, that is, the ministers of religion, who are its guardians, appointed for this purpose, that it may suffer nothing to decay. The second is that they themselves should keep within the bounds of those rites which both God has prescribed and those ministers keep, and not loosen the reins on their own nature, which is inclined to wander. The third is that they should hold to the pure Word of God, not bent by bad examples or by a perverse exposition.

units.la: In quarum rationum curam atq; studium nobis hoc præsertim tam deperdito tamq; deplorato tempore est etiam incumbendum, ne quod videmus pasim fieri nos etiam à verbi diuini veritate in papisticas tenebras retrahamur. Et certe hæ nobis ad id cauendum non minus proderunt, quam illis Jsraelitis ad vitandas Cananaicas superstitiones, obtinendam-que legem Dei, si modo eas sigillatim singulas suo modo ponderemus. Tractat autem pri-mum de Leuitis, tum de exercitio, deniq; de verbi feruanda puritate.
units.tr: To the care and zeal for these reasons we too must especially apply ourselves in this so lost and so deplorable time, lest, as we see happening everywhere, we also be drawn back from the truth of the divine Word into Papist darkness. And these reasons will surely help us to guard against this no less than they helped those Israelites to avoid Canaanite superstitions and to keep the law of God, if only we weigh each of them singly in its own way. He treats first of the Levites, then of the exercise of religion, and finally of keeping the Word pure.

units.la: Ac de Leuitis quidem fovendis ad hunc modum disserit: Caue ne forte deferas Leuitas, &c. Erant autem Leuitæ ministri religionis & cerimoniarum: nec opus est de eorum origine, ordine, vestibus dicere, quando cum locus erit de iis dicetur postea, in præsentia autem a-gitur de eorum officio, quasi causa, propter quam Moses eos nolit deseri.
units.tr: Concerning the cherishing of the Levites he speaks in this manner: Take heed lest perhaps you neglect the Levites, etc. Now the Levites were ministers of religion and of the ceremonies. Nor is it necessary to speak of their origin, order and vestments, since that will be said in its place later; for the present the matter concerns their office, as the reason why Moses does not want them forsaken.

units.la: Quid igitur est deferere quempiam? Est eum qui nostra habet opus opera negligere, nostrisque officijs ut amictu, victu, defensione destituere, veluti pater eum dicitur relinquere filium, quem sua domo, suo conuictu prohibet, suis consilijs & auxilijs destituit.
units.tr: What then is it to forsake someone? It is to neglect one who has need of our work, and to deprive him of our services, such as clothing, food and protection; just as a father is said to abandon a son whom he shuts out of his house and from his company, and leaves without his counsel and help.

units.la: Quod si Leuitis accidat, locus illis in populi cœtu manendi nullus erat reliquus. At Moses illos manere voluit, ecqua de causa? ut eas res obirent quibus gerendis erant destinati.
units.tr: If this should happen to the Levites, no place would remain for them to stay in the assembly of the people. But Moses wanted them to remain. For what reason? So that they might perform those duties for which they had been appointed.

units.la: Erat autem eorum primum docere: sic enim Leuit. 10. diĉtum est Aharoni & illius fi-lijs: ut doceatis filios Jsrael omnia statuta, quæ locutus est Dominus per ministerium Mosis. Alterum erat benedicere, de quo Num.6. scriptum est. Tertium erat sacra facere & sacrorum atq; templi custodes esse. Ex quo perspicuum est eos retinendæ religioni fuisse omnium ma-xime deputatos atq; etiam idoneos.
units.tr: Now their first duty was to teach, for so it is said in Leviticus 10 to Aaron and his sons: that you may teach the children of Israel all the statutes which the Lord has spoken by the ministry of Moses. The second was to bless, of which it is written in Numbers 6. The third was to perform the sacred rites and to be the keepers of the sacred things and of the temple. From this it is clear that they were chosen and fitted above all for maintaining religion.

units.la: Jam cum eos Moses ad conseruandam religionem sustentari præcipiat: in eo quid nobis expediat cernimus, nempe ut ad retinendam religionis puritatem nihil perinde conducat, ac si verbi ministros non deferamus. Vere enim est diĉtum, honos alit artes. Jam si videas ver-bi ministros & contemni & odio haberi quid præsagias aliud quàm eius quam tradunt ar-tis, hoc est, religionis apud nos ruinam? Ac vides ni bonis publicis educarentur ad ea studia quidam juvenes: periculum esse ne non eorum inopia laboraremus maxima. Tum videmus ut iis ministrantibus victum illi quoq; invideant, qui ipsis ne terunciũ[?] conferunt. Cur non potius cogitant male feriati homines iure eum ali ex publico, qui suos labores omnes impen-dit reipublicæ? iure eum, ut ait apostolus, ex altari vivere, qui ipse etiam altari seruiat? Et cer-te Christus ait, Dignus est operarius mercede sua.
units.tr: Since Moses commands that they be supported in order to preserve religion, we see what is useful for us in this: namely, that nothing contributes so much to keeping the purity of religion as not forsaking the ministers of the Word. For it is rightly said that honour nourishes the arts. Now if you see the ministers of the Word both despised and held in hatred, what do you foresee but the ruin of that art which they teach, that is, of religion among us? And do you not see that some young men are not brought up at public expense for these studies? There is danger that we will suffer the greatest lack of them. Then we see that those who give the ministers nothing, not even a farthing, begrudge them their food. Why do idle men not rather consider that it is right for him to be supported from the public purse who spends all his labours on the commonwealth? Is it not right, as the Apostle says, that he who serves at the altar should live from the altar? And indeed Christ says: The labourer is worthy of his wages.

units.la: Nec est quod vllo se quærantur onere supprimi, cum illis nemo det nisi quod debetur: invidia fit hoc totum quod dicimus. Quo nam agitante? sane satana: quare vero? ut religionis cognitione genus nostrum exuat. Magna est enim naturæ nostræ ad ἐθελοθρησκείαν[?] propen-sio, contra hanc ministri ceu custodes dati. His satan homines ceu agnos canibus destitutos lupus solet, improvisos obruit.
units.tr: Nor have they any reason to complain that they are weighed down by a burden, since no one gives them anything but what is owed. All this that we say is stirred up by envy. By whom is it stirred? Surely by Satan. Why? So that he may strip our race of the knowledge of religion. For our nature has a great propensity to self-devised worship [ἐθελοθρησκεία], and against this ministers have been given as guardians. Satan is accustomed to fall upon men, as a wolf falls upon lambs left without dogs, and to overwhelm them when they are unprepared.

units.la: Ac certe præsens imminebat iis periculum, qui suis pastoribus carerent. Pharao iubet abire Mosem & Aharonem ut destitutum his ducibus populum sub iugo retineret. Populus absente Mose per diabolum seduci potuit, ut aureum vitulum erigeret. Samuele valere iusso declinat & perit Saulus. Profligatis cum Helia prophetis omnibus Baal in Jsrael colitur. Ut Herodem in turpi incesto retineret satan Baptistam monitorem opera scelestæ meretricis obtruncat. Judæi Christo & apostolis domitis videbantur populum dementare posse. Julia-nus sublatis è medio scholis & doctoribus religionem facile euersurus esse videbatur. In pap-patu submotis pastoribus & eorum loco positis statuis atq; canibus, populus deceptus est falsa doctrina.
units.tr: And indeed the danger was at hand for those who lacked their pastors. Pharaoh bade Moses and Aaron depart, so that he might keep the people under the yoke, deprived of these leaders. In Moses' absence the people could be seduced by the devil to set up the golden calf. When Samuel had been bidden farewell, Saul turned aside and perished. When all the prophets were destroyed along with Elijah, Baal was worshipped in Israel. To keep Herod in shameful incest, Satan had the Baptist, his reprover, beheaded through the work of a wicked harlot. The Jews, once Christ and the apostles were subdued, seemed able to drive the people mad. Julian, once the schools and teachers were removed from the midst, seemed about to overthrow religion with ease. In the Papacy, when the pastors were removed and statues and dogs were set in their place, the people were deceived by false doctrine.

units.la: Jam communis omnium querela est nobis è medio sublatis posse fieri concordiam, quos vero psassos[?] putat tollendos è medio? nō eos, qui sunt ac nominantur psassi[?]: hos enim olim eiectos nunc reuocatos restituunt in integrum: sed nos qui ipsum prædicamus euangelium. Ergo si tibi velis prædicari euangelium, caue hos deferas. Noli male sanos affectus pluris æstimare quam salutem tuam: ac si castigatus doleas, medere adhibitis pœnitentia & fide, & conualesces, & noles postea non factum. Oportet hos habeas custodes veræ fidei.
units.tr: Now it is the common complaint of everyone that concord cannot be made once the psassi are removed from the midst. But whom does he think should be removed? Not those who are and are called psassi, for these, though once cast out, are now recalled and restored to their former state. Rather, it is us who preach the gospel itself. So if you wish the gospel to be preached to you, take care not to hand these over. Do not value diseased affections above your salvation. If, when rebuked, you grieve, apply repentance and faith as remedies, and you will recover, and afterwards you will not wish that the thing had not been done. You must have these as guardians of true faith.

units.la: Sed quid tu? num rem omnem remittes sacerdotibus, ut papistæ concilijs, & episcopis suis confessores timidi? Quin tuam quoque verbo retinendo præstabis operam. Id iam do-cet Moses.
units.tr: But what about you? Will you leave the whole matter to the priests, as the Papists leave it to councils, and timid confessors leave it to their bishops? Indeed, you too should lend your effort to retaining the word. Moses already teaches this.

units.la: Acceptæ religionis exercitio, quod ut commendet & inculcet amplius, locum, sacra, for-mam iterum commemorat, docens iis standum, ab iisq; ne pedem unum discedendum.
units.tr: In the exercise of the religion received, which he commends and presses home more firmly, he recalls once again the place, the sacred things and the form, teaching that one must stand by them and not depart from them by a single step.

units.la: Quo discimus enitendum esse, ut diuinitus accepta mordicus retineamus, eaque noctes atque dies versemus. Quo plus precatus fueris, hoc plus precaberis: quò minus incumbes precibus, hoc minus illis delectabere. Idem in verbi audiendi studio & in sacramentorum v-su spectandum est: quæ sunt legis loco posita Christianis exercitia. Adam obliuione & negligentia præcepti peccauit: qui lapsus patriarchas eius posteros perpulit, uti postea se su-osque domi suæ tanquam in scholis exercerent. Et Deus hunc Mosaicum cultum ideo instituit, uti illo ipso religionis negligentiam pelleret. Et Christus submotis uti prædictum erat, umbris & figuris, aliqua populo Christiano reliquit exercitia, ea videlicet de quibus diximus. Dauid autem publicis conuentibus, quibus fides exerceretur, plurimum tribuit. Ex quibus intelligi potest quid ad conseruandam religionem populi referat facere.
units.tr: From this we learn that we must strive to hold fast to what has been received from God and to keep turning it over night and day. The more you have prayed, the more you will be drawn to pray; the less you apply yourself to prayer, the less you will delight in it. The same must be observed in the eagerness to hear the word and in the use of the sacraments, which have been set in place of the law as exercises for Christians. Adam sinned through forgetfulness and neglect of the precept. That fall drove his patriarchs and posterity to exercise themselves and their households at home, as in schools. God instituted this Mosaic worship so that it would drive out negligence of religion itself. And Christ, once the shadows and figures had been removed, as had been foretold, left the Christian people certain exercises, namely those of which we have spoken. David, moreover, attached great weight to public assemblies, in which faith is exercised. From these things it can be understood how much it matters for preserving the religion of the people that they be diligent in doing it.

units.la: Verbi Dei pura ac syncera doctrina, dicit, Obserua & custodi omnia præcepta, &c. Quibus docet verbum ipsum sic retinendum, vt purum putum habeatur: ac ne qua fiat impostura cauendum ne vel exemplis, vel sinistra expositione detorqueatur. Exempli vice Cananæos habere poterant: eorum superstitiones deuitandas esse docuit. Vtinam in ecclesiam non etiam Iudæos & Romanos ritus inuexissent Romani pontifices, ac fecissent vt ecclesia haberet omnia pristino gentilismo similima. Sed ab his exemplis abstinendum Mosesd docet vt verbum Dei purum habeamus.
units.tr: Of the pure and sincere doctrine of God's word, he says: "Observe and keep all the precepts, etc." By this he teaches that the word itself must be retained in such a way that it is held pure and unmixed, and that care must be taken lest any deception arise, lest it be twisted either by examples or by a perverse exposition. The Canaanites could serve as the example; he taught that their superstitions are to be avoided. Would that the Roman pontiffs had not introduced Jewish and Roman rites into the Church, and made the Church have everything most like the old paganism. But Moses teaches that we must abstain from such examples, so that we may have the word of God pure.

units.la: Tum ne vitietur, expositione dicit; nempe vt ei vel addas aliquid, vel detrahas. Nam scripturæ simpliciter mentem sequi virtutis est: sed ei vel aliquid addere vel detrahere in vitio est.
units.tr: Then, lest it be corrupted, he adds the matter of exposition; that is, that one should add something to it or take something away from it. For to follow the mind of Scripture simply is a virtue, but to add to it or subtract from it is a vice.

units.la: Quod sit ad hunc modum. Non facies tibi sculptile: huic plus addis si imaginum earum, quæ non coluntur, nec religionis causa ponuntur, vsu prohibeas: neq; enim Deus has vetuit: rursus detrahis ei si Christi, sanctorum martyrum idola concessa putes, ac gentilia tantum di cas vetita, cum Deus nullarum neq; cœlestium, neq; terrestrium, neq; etiam inferarum rerum imagines esse religioni voluerit. Ne sumas nomen Dei tui vanè. Ei legi additur si iuramentum quoq; per hanc tolli dicas: neq; enim Deus ipsum prohibuit: rursus ei detrahitur, si per missas doceas eas, quæ per alias res quascunq; creatas vt terram, cœlum, & reliqua fiunt, peie rationes: quas tamen Christo teste Deus etiam ipsas vetuit. Lex est, non occides: qui ne latronem quidem trucidari seu plecti volunt, ij quiddam amplius, quam Deus vetuerit, addunt: rursus qui veritatis causa pios atq; innocentes occidunt, ij detrahunt legi, qua Deus hoc scelere cum priuatos homines, tum ipsos etiam magistratus prohibuit.
units.tr: This works as follows. "You shall not make for yourself a graven image." You add to this law if you forbid the use of those images which are not worshipped and are not set up for the sake of religion, for God did not forbid these. Again, you subtract from it if you think the images of Christ and of the holy martyrs are permitted, and say that only the pagan images are forbidden, since God did not want images of any things, heavenly, earthly or even of things below, to be objects of religion. "You shall not take the name of your God in vain." A thing is added to this law if you say that swearing too is removed by it, for God did not forbid swearing itself. Again, it is subtracted from it if you teach that those oaths which are sworn by other created things, such as earth, heaven and the rest, are perjuries, whereas God, with Christ as witness, forbade even these. The law says "You shall not kill." Those who do not want even a robber to be slain or punished add something beyond what God forbade. Again, those who kill pious and innocent people for the sake of truth subtract from the law, by which God forbade this crime both to private persons and to the magistrates themselves.

units.la: Qua de causa adhibenda ad scripturæ expositionem est charitatis atque fidei regula, ita vt ipsius semper stetur iudicio. Quod si fiat verbum ipsum purum semper retinebimus. Id faxit Deus per Iesum Christum. Amen.
units.tr: For this reason the rule of charity and faith must be applied to the exposition of Scripture, so that one always abides by its judgment. If this is done, we shall always keep the word itself pure. May God grant this through Jesus Christ. Amen.

units.la: CAPUT XIII. SERMO XXIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XIII. SERMON XXIII.

units.la: Si surrexerit in medio tui propheta, aut qui somnium somniet, dederitq; tibi aut signum aut portentum.
units.tr: If there arise in the midst of thee a prophet, or one that dreameth a dream, and giveth thee a sign or a wonder.

units.la: 2 Euenerit&q;[?] signum & portentum, quod prædixit tibi, atque vt dixerit, eamus post deos alios (quos non nouisti) & seruiemus eis:
units.tr: 2 And the sign or wonder come to pass, which he foretold thee, and he say, Let us go after other gods (whom thou hast not known), and let us serve them:

units.la: 3 Non audies verba prophetæ illius qui somniauerit huiusmodi somnium, quia tentat vos Dominus Deus vester num fitis amantes Domini Dei vestri in toto corde vestro, & in tota anima vestra.
units.tr: 3 Thou shalt not hear the words of that prophet, or of that dreamer of such a dream: for the Lord your God tempteth you, that he may know whether you love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul.

units.la: 4 Incedite post Dominum Deum vestrum, illum timete, illius præcepta custodite, illius vocem audite, illi seruite atque illi adhærete.
units.tr: 4 Walk after the Lord your God, fear him, keep his commandments, hear his voice, serve him, and cleave to him.

units.la: 5 Propheta autem talis, aut somniorum somniator interfici debet, eo quod de-sectionem loquutus fit à Domino Deo vestro (qui eduxit vos de terra Ægypti, & redemit te de domo seruitutis) vt te depelleret à via, quam præscripsit tibi Dominus Deus tuus, vt in ea ambulares, & ideo exterminabis malum è medio tui.
units.tr: 5 But that prophet, or dreamer of dreams, shall be put to death, because he hath spoken of revolt from the Lord your God (who brought you out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed you out of the house of bondage), to thrust you out of the way which the Lord your God commanded you to walk in: and so thou shalt take away the evil from the midst of thee.

units.la: N[?]fine præcedentis Cap. ostendit Moses ad conseruandum verū & simplicem cultum Dei requiri potissimum, vt primum Leuitæ ceu magistri & custodes religionis foueantur: tùm ipse populus in eo subinde sese exerceat, quo hoc ipso tum optime imbuatur, tum etiam subinde suauius ac suauius afficiatur: deniq; vt ipsa doctrina, ceu eius gubernatrix & domina prorsus illibata, pura puta, ac qualis diuinitus est exhibita, sic in cœtu populi retineatur. Iam vero in sequenti 13. Cap. docet huc etiam momenti plurimum afferri pseudoprophetarum proffigatione: nempe vt caueatur sedulo, ne qui malis artibus ab ipso Dei cultu, ab eius vsu atq; exercitio, deniq; etiam ab ipsa verbi Dei puritate populum seducant atq; alienent. Ac quo magis tutus fit coetus populi praecipit ex mandato Dei prophetas eos e medio tol lendos esse, ne latius serpat a paucis in vniuersos malum.
units.tr: At the end of the preceding chapter Moses shows that, to preserve the true and simple worship of God, it is above all required that the Levites, as teachers and guardians of religion, be cherished; then that the people themselves exercise themselves in it, by which very means they are both best instructed and from time to time more and more sweetly moved; and finally that doctrine itself, as its guide and mistress, be kept in the assembly of the people wholly unimpaired, pure, that is, just as it has been divinely delivered. Now in the following thirteenth chapter he teaches that much is also contributed to this by the overthrow of false prophets: namely, that care be taken diligently lest by evil arts they seduce and alienate the people from the very worship of God, from its use and practice, and finally from the very purity of the Word of God. And so that the assembly of the people may be safer, he commands by God's order that these prophets be removed from the midst, lest evil creep more widely from a few to all.

units.la: Sed quonam satan multos habet & varios errorum satores: ac modo ductores mittat quorum opera publice magnos coetus ad se trahat, modo clandestinos errorum magistros, qui clam religioni detrahant, in priuata conuenticula submittat: atque etiam magnas respublicas, quarum vi potentiaq; falsum muniatur, occupet: Moses ea genera omnia commemo rat, & quid de quoq; sit ex verbo Dei statuendum exponit.
units.tr: But since Satan has many and various sowers of error, and sends now leaders by whose work he draws great assemblies to himself in public, now secret teachers of error who undermine religion in private, and places them in private conventicles; and even seizes great commonwealths, by whose power and strength falsehood is fortified: Moses recalls all these kinds and sets out what is to be determined about each from the Word of God.

units.la: Ac primum quidem de magistris falsae doctrinae satoribus, quid Deo videatur tripartito monstrat: primum videlicet dicens de persona, tum de eorum factis & doctrina, postremo quomodo cauendi sint & coercendi.
units.tr: And first, concerning the teachers and sowers of false doctrine, he shows in three parts what seems good to God: first speaking of their person, then of their deeds and doctrine, and lastly of how they are to be guarded against and restrained.

units.la: Ac de persona quidem ad hunc modum dicit: Si surrexerit in medio tui propheta, aut qui somnium somniet. Quibus verbis duo potisima pseudoprophetarum genera commemorat: vnum eorum quos prophetas vocat, alterum eorum quos somniatores appellat.
units.tr: Concerning the person he speaks thus: If there arise in the midst of thee a prophet, or one that dreameth a dream. By these words he recalls two principal kinds of false prophets: one of those whom he calls prophets, the other of those whom he calls dreamers.

units.la: Prophetis primum locum tribuit. Est autem prophetae nomen Graecum & significat, eum, qui praedicit quae sunt post euentura. Et [?]נָבִיא[?] vox Hebraea ab eo verbo deduci videtur quod significat procreationem seu productionem frugum. Quod quemadmodum fruges, vel in terra, vel in plantis vel in vitibus primum quidem latent, deinceps autem a natura procreatrice proferuntur, ac iuuant: sic consilia primum quidem in hominum animis latent, tum autem oratione & verbis efferuntur. Quod genus proferendi & perspicuum faciendi propterea prophetis vere & proprie tribuitur, quod nihil perinde lateat, atque arcana Dei consilia, quorum illi sunt precones & interpretes. Et hoc ipsum magis ex eo perspicuum est ita se habere, quod verbum illud interdum passiue positum significat prophetas etiam sibi ipsis incognita ac diuinitus prodita dicere.
units.tr: He gives the first place to prophets. The name prophet is Greek and signifies one who foretells what is to come afterwards. The Hebrew word navi [נָבִיא] also seems to be derived from the verb that signifies the bringing forth or production of fruits. Just as fruits, whether in the earth, or in plants or vines, lie hidden at first and afterwards are brought forth and aided by the productive nature, so counsels lie hidden at first in men's minds and then are brought out in speech and words. This kind of bringing forth and making manifest is therefore truly and properly attributed to prophets, because nothing lies hidden in the way God's secret counsels do, and the prophets are their heralds and interpreters. This is the more evident from the fact that the verb, sometimes used in the passive, signifies that prophets also speak things unknown to themselves and divinely revealed.

units.la: Vnde & Philo ille doctissimus Hebraeo rū philosophus prophetam definiens ait: [?]ἑρμηνεὺς γὰρ ὁ προφήτης ἐνδοτὴν ὑπηχούων[?] [?]τὰ λεκτέα τῷ θεῷ[?]. Ex quibus est perspicuum prophetam eum dici, qui diuina mysteria, quae naturae viribus aliàs assequi non possumus, siue praesentia, siue praeterita, siue futura fuerint, diuinitus sibi patefacta reddit atq; exponit. Quo pertinent rerum futurarum praedictiones, vt illae Iacobi patriarchae, Danielis, Agabi & aliorum. Eodem referuntur etiam eorum concionesQ & officia, qui diuinitus extra ordinem mittuntur ad reformandos corruptos magistratus, sacerdotes, atque populos, quales fuerunt Moses, Samuel, Helias, Helizeus, Esaias, Hieremias & alij. Nec sunt alieni ab isto ordine Sacrae scripturae interpretes, qui locos obscuros eius à quo sunt proditi spiritus ductu plenius exponunt & ad vsum hominum exponunt. Ex quibus intelligimus omnes doctores, Ecclesiarum ministros, & qui praesunt ecclesiis hoc nomine censeri.
units.tr: Hence also that most learned philosopher of the Hebrews, Philo, in defining a prophet says: "For the prophet is an interpreter, echoing back the things to be said by God" [ἑρμηνεὺς γὰρ ὁ προφήτης ἐνδοτὴν ὑπηχούων τὰ λεκτέα τῷ θεῷ]. From these things it is clear that he is called a prophet who renders and sets forth divine mysteries, which we cannot otherwise attain by the powers of nature, whether they concern the present, the past or the future, and who has them revealed to him by God. To this belong predictions of future things, such as those of the patriarch Jacob, of Daniel, of Agabus and others. To the same belong also the sermons and offices of those who are sent by God outside the ordinary order to reform corrupt magistrates, priests and peoples, such as Moses, Samuel, Elijah, Elisha, Isaiah, Jeremiah and others. Nor are the interpreters of Holy Scripture foreign to this order, who by the guidance of the Spirit by whom it was given expound more fully its obscure passages and set them out for the use of men. From these things we understand that all teachers, ministers of the Churches, and those who preside over the congregations are counted under this name.

units.la: Iam quemadmodum Deus prophetarum opera verbi sui semen spargit & quae sit ad beatam vitam recta via patefacit: sic satan prophetas falsos suis mendacijs afflatos clam in hominum coetus submittit, ac quos potest vana veri specie deceptos perdit. Hi satanae legati nomen, & doctrinae genus cum prophetis bonis vnum idemque praetendunt, sed interpre tatione multum deflectunt. Veluti nostra aetate videmus fieri, vt anabaptistae & papistae nō mi nus scripturas afferant, quam doctores Christiani: veluti iam inde à Christi temporibus vsu compertum est omnes haereticos suis erroribus scripturas asciuisse tuendis. Sed Moses iussu Dei monet, quo loco sint hoc genus prophetae habendi.
units.tr: Now just as God through his prophets scatters the seed of his Word and opens the right way to a blessed life, so Satan secretly sends into the assemblies of men false prophets, inspired by his lies, and destroys those whom he can deceive by the empty semblance of truth. These legates of Satan put forward the same name and kind of doctrine as the good prophets, but differ greatly in their interpretation. As we see happening in our own age, Anabaptists and Papists bring forward Scripture no less than Christian teachers do; as has been found by experience from the very times of Christ, all heretics have claimed Scripture to defend their errors. But Moses, by God's command, warns in what cases this kind of prophet is to be held.

units.la: Alterum genus eorum est, quos à somnijs quae proponunt, somniatores vocat. Neq; vero hoc ipso reijcit omnia somnia: est enim eorum quoddam genus diuinum, vt illud Pharao nis, vxoris Pilati, Gabiniani illius apud Augustinum, & nonnulla alia: quae quoniam sunt immortalis Dei munus, & saepe magnis calamitatibus auertendis seruiunt: tantum est vt contemnenda sint, vt etiam maximi fieri debeant.
units.tr: The other kind is those whom he calls dreamers, from the dreams they propose. Yet he does not thereby reject all dreams: there is a certain divine kind of dream, such as that of Pharaoh, that of Pilate's wife, that of Gabinianus in Augustine, and some others. Since these are an immortal gift of God and often serve to avert great calamities, they are so far from being despised that they ought rather to be held in the highest esteem.

units.la: Sed sunt alia quaedam vana & dubia, vt quae vel ex temperie bona malaue corporum, vel ex rerum diurnarum recursu nasci consueuere: veluti si redundante phlegmate multas atque pluuias, aut superante melancholia tristia somnies: ea nihili sunt ac videntur omnibus somnia.
units.tr: But there are certain other dreams, empty and doubtful, such as those which usually arise from a good or bad temperament of the body, or from the recurrence of the day's affairs: for example, if from excess of phlegm you dream of many showers, or from excess of melancholy you dream of sad things. These are nothing, and everyone sees them as mere dreams.

units.la: Vnde existit vt rebus incertis & dubijs & omnino omnibus opinione magis, quam certa ac solida cognitione satis somniorum nomen attribuamus. Veluti Lucianus in Harmonide nūgas dicens, [illegible, ~45 letters] (inquit) [illegible, ~30 letters]. Atq; hæc quí dem à verbis etiam ad ipsos homines est tradu&ta ratio, nempe vt homines nihili boni scri-ptores vocent somnia: vt Terentianus Syrus Demeam suum coràm vehens laudibus dicat, ipsum quantus quantus sit nihil nisi sapientia: Mitionem autem illum esse futilem, somniū.
units.tr: Hence it comes about that we apply the name of dreams to uncertain and doubtful things, and altogether to all things that rest more on opinion than on sure and solid knowledge. So Lucian, in the Harmonides, calling trifles... [text illegible in scan] (he says) [text illegible in scan]. This manner of speaking has indeed passed from words to men themselves, so that writers call worthless men dreams: as Terentianus Syrus, lauding his Demea to his face, says that he himself, however great he is, is nothing but wisdom, while Micio is futile, a dream.

units.la: Sic Moses istos impostores & eorum dogmata somnijs comparat, quod cum se fuaq; dogmata nec ratione recta, nec scripturæ testimonijs tueri posint: ad nescio quas visiones, reuelationes, & diuinos afflatus confugiant. Veluti patrum nostrorum memoria monachi & sa-crifici purgatorium nescio quibus animarum apparitionibus, somnijs, visionibus magis, quá scripturis sacris obtinuerunt. At eiusmodi spiritus etiam apostolus cauendos esse docuit, cū Galatis scriberet nec angelum cœlitus delapsum, quando quid diuersum ab euangelio nun ciaret, audiendum.
units.tr: Thus Moses compares those impostors and their doctrines to dreams, because since they cannot defend themselves and their doctrines either by sound reason or by the testimonies of Scripture, they flee to I know not what visions, revelations and divine inspirations. Thus within the memory of our fathers, monks and sacrificing priests established purgatory by I know not what apparitions of souls, dreams and visions, rather than by the holy Scriptures. But the apostle also taught that such spirits are to be avoided, when in writing to the Galatians he said that not even an angel come down from heaven was to be heard if he announced anything different from the gospel.

units.la: Atq; sic prophetas & somniatores deuitandos Moses asserit, eorumq; nomine reliquos impostores omnes siue se scripturis male tortis, siue reuelationibus tueantur, comprehedit.
units.tr: And so Moses declares that prophets and dreamers are to be avoided, and by this name he embraces all the other impostors, whether they defend their claims by twisting Scripture or by revelations.

units.la: Cæterum, vt Christus monuit Matth. 7. ex fructibus agnoscemus eos, propterea q; eorū fructus iam describit.
units.tr: Moreover, as Christ warned in Matthew 7, we shall know them by their fruits, and therefore Moses goes on to describe those fruits.

units.la: De dictis & de factis eorum sic dicit, Si, inquit, dederit signū aut portentum, & euenerit, &c. etdixerit, Eamus post deos alienos, &c. Quibus verbis ostenditillorum opera atq; dogmata, vt ex ijs quasi fructibus qui qualesq; sint posit æstimari. Ac sunt eorum opera magna, nempe signa & portenta, quæ cum supra naturam sint, obijciunt animis quasi quandam potentiæ maioris significationem. Eius generis sunt quæ magi Ægyptij, Sophi gentiles, Simon magus, nonnulli Romani pontifices fecere: quæ quandoq; falsa ac vana, quandoq; vi rerum creatarum, plerunq; ope & inductria satanæ efficiuntur. Iam ne seducamur Christus & apostoli prædicunt has fallacias, & vt ab ijs cauëamus monent, Matth. 24. 2. Thess. 2.
units.tr: He speaks of their words and deeds thus: "If he gives a sign or a wonder, and it comes to pass, etc., and says, 'Let us go after other gods,' etc." By these words he shows their works and doctrines, so that from these fruits, as it were, one may judge what sort of people they are. Their works are indeed great, namely signs and wonders, which, since they lie beyond nature, present to minds a kind of token of greater power. Of this kind are the wonders wrought by the Egyptian magicians, the Gentile sages, Simon Magus, and some Roman pontiffs. Sometimes these are false and empty, sometimes they are produced by the force of created things, but most often by the help and industry of Satan. Lest we be deceived, Christ and the apostles foretell these deceits and warn us to beware of them: Matthew 24; 2 Thessalonians 2.

units.la: Doctrinam autem dicit summatim hoc agere, vt post deos alienos eatur. Atq; hæc est falsi nota certissima, qua audita vel subodorata quid quid dixerint statim omnę respuendū, Nam hæc est prima ac princeps diuinarum legum omnium quæ Deum vnum & solum adorandum præcipit. Ab hac si quis te velit abducere, actum est ilicet. Hanc notam in omni cū gentilium, tum papisticarum superstitionum genere seruandam meminerimus.
units.tr: Moses says that such a teacher's whole aim is to lead men after other gods. This is the most certain mark of falsehood: once it is heard or even suspected, whatever such a person has said must be rejected at once. For this is the first and chief of all the divine laws, which commands that the one and only God alone be worshipped. If anyone tries to draw you away from this, it is all over for you. Let us remember that this mark must be observed in every kind of superstition, both Gentile and Papist.

units.la: Sed quod Moses doctrinam simul & miracula refert, argumento est miracula recipien-da non esse, quæ falsæ doctrinæ stabiliendæ causa fiunt. Præclarè est enim à D. Paulo scriptū, vt ne quod angelus cœlitus demissus, ab eo quod iam didicissent euangelio diuersum afferret, reciperent.
units.tr: But that Moses reports doctrine and miracles together is a proof that miracles wrought in order to establish false doctrine are not to be received. For St. Paul wrote well that even if an angel came down from heaven and brought something different from the gospel they had already learned, they were not to receive it.

units.la: Quomodo verò cauendi & coercendi sint, ad hunc modum dicit, Non audies, &c. Sum ma non vult audiri quod alienum est à vero: idq; probat argumentis minime malis, nempe, vt quid & de eo ipso impostorum genere & de te fieri Deo placeat, intelligas. De te, vt hoc genus homines non audias, hoc est vt respuas, repudies: id est enim tutissimum. Euæ nocuit audisse serpentem. Syrenas obturatis auribus Vlysses præternauigauit. Ergo memineris abstinendum.
units.tr: As for how such people are to be guarded against and restrained, he says in this way: "You shall not listen, etc." In sum, he does not wish what is foreign to the truth to be heard. He proves this by arguments that are by no means weak, namely so that you may understand both what kind of impostor this is and what God wishes done about you. About you: that you should not listen to this kind of people, that is, that you should reject and refuse them, for that is the safest course. Eve was harmed by listening to the serpent. Ulysses sailed past the Sirens with his ears stopped. Therefore remember that you must abstain.

units.la: Sed Moses ipse rationes affert. 1. à fine quem Deus in pseudoprophetia respicit. Tentat vos, inquit; Dominus Deus vester, num illum ametis. An quia nescitur? Minime vero nescit hoc qui scit omnia: sed vt nos, qui nesciebamus hoc ipsum cognoscæremus. Ex quo perspicuum est eum persecutionum omnium & calamitatum, quas immittit Deus, finem esse, vt nostrer [?] in illum amor patefiat. Exemplo sunt Iob, Abraham, Petrus, apostoli: in quibus quæ latebât, patefacta sunt. Quæ cum ita sint nec pseudoprophetarum studijs [?], nec copia quenquam offendendi fas est: eum tam bonus finis à Deo respiciatur. Quin illis nec locum nec aures præbe.
units.tr: But Moses himself gives reasons. (1) From the end which God has in view in the false prophecy. "The Lord your God," he says, "tests you, whether you love him." Is it because God does not know? By no means: he who knows all things does not lack knowledge; rather it is so that we, who did not know it, might come to know it. From this it is clear that the end of all the persecutions and calamities which God sends is that our love for him might be made manifest. Job, Abraham, Peter and the apostles are examples: what lay hidden in them was brought to light. Since this is so, it is not right to yield to the enticements of false prophets or to the number of those who may offend, when God has so good an end in view. Rather, do not give them either place or ear.

units.la: 2. A nostro officio: Incedite post Deum vestrum. Enumeratione partium officium noftrū describit. Sequi Deum est illum timere, eius præcepta custodire, illum audire, illi seruire, illi relictis rebus omnibus adhærere. Vnde sequitur, ne falsos magistros sequamur, creaturas timeamus, humanas traditiones seruemus, dijs qui non sunt obsequamur. Atque hæc quidem ad nos, quibus hoc hominum genus causandum est pertinent.
units.tr: (2) From our duty: "Walk after the Lord your God." By enumerating the parts, he describes our duty. To follow God is to fear him, keep his precepts, hear him, serve him, and cling to him with all things left behind. Hence it follows that we must not follow false teachers, must not fear creatures, must not keep human traditions, and must not obey gods that are not gods. These things pertain to us, for whom this kind of man is to be shunned.

units.la: De illis autem pseudoprophetis dicit: Propheta autem talis interfici debet, &c. Pœna videtur grauis? Quibusdam vt Augustino quondam secus videtur. Sed vt illi rem postea secus putanti, quod hic Moses dicit magis placebit.
units.tr: Concerning those false prophets he says: "But such a prophet must be put to death, etc." Does the penalty seem severe? To some, such as Augustine once, it seemed otherwise. But what Moses says here will please more, as it did Augustine when he later judged the matter differently.

units.la: Rationes affert: Quia talis locutus est defectionem à Deo. Magnum hoc scelus est. Etenim si quis in ciuitate res nouas moliatur, homines à magistratu ad suas partes alliciat capitis reus est. Si quis humanas tabulas deprauaret magnum est: quid de diuinis? Ac ne frigeat argumē tu,addit,quis fit Deus:qui eduxit & redemit.2.a via diuinitus praescripta,à qua non erat abes-randum.3.malum exterminandum ceu pestis, ne serpat latius. Ex quibus rursus intelligi po-teft quam cauendum fit quod abducit à Deo,cum fit enitendum, vt Deo semper coniun-cti beatissimus.Amen.
units.tr: He gives reasons: "Because he has spoken of defection from God." This is a great crime. Indeed, if anyone in a city plots revolution and draws men from the magistrate to his own party, he is liable to capital punishment. If anyone corrupts human documents, that is a serious matter: what then of divine ones? And lest the argument grow cold, he adds who God is: he who brought us out and redeemed us. (2) From the way prescribed by God, from which one must not depart. (3) The evil must be destroyed like a plague, lest it creep further. From these things one may again understand how carefully we must beware of what draws us away from God, since we must strive always to be most blessedly joined to God. Amen.

units.la: SERMO XXIIII.
units.tr: SERMON XXIIII.

units.la: 6 Si te clanculum folicitauerit frater tuus filius matris tuæ,aut filius tuus,aut filia tua,aut vxor gremij tui,aut proximus quem vt propriam vitam(amas) dicet do,Eamus & seruiamus dijs alijs,quos nec tu nouisti,nec patres tui.
units.tr: 6 If your brother, the son of your mother, or your son, or your daughter, or the wife of your bosom, or your neighbour whom you love as your own life, secretly entice you, saying: Let us go and serve other gods, whom neither you nor your fathers have known.

units.la: 7 Fuerintque ex dijs populorum, qui circum vos sunt, siue propè fuerint te-cum,siue procul à te,ab vna extremitate terræ,ad aliam extremitatem terræ.
units.tr: 7 Namely, of the gods of the peoples which are round about you, whether nigh unto thee or far off from thee, from the one end of the earth even unto the other end of the earth;

units.la: 8 Ne acquiescas ei,neq; audies eum,nec parcat ei oculus tuus, neq; indulgeas, neq; abscondas eum.
units.tr: 8 Thou shalt not consent unto him, nor hearken unto him; neither shall thine eye pity him, neither shalt thou spare, neither shalt thou conceal him:

units.la: 9 Sed omnino occidas eum,& manus tua prima sit in eo vt occidatur talis, deinde & manus totius populi.
units.tr: 9 But thou shalt surely kill him; thine hand shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterward the hand of all the people.

units.la: 10 Obrues eum lapidibus donec moriatur,hoc enim molitus est, vt depelleret te à Domino Deo tuo,qui te eduxit de terra Ægypti,de domo seruitutis.
units.tr: 10 And thou shalt stone him with stones, that he die; because he hath sought to thrust thee away from the LORD thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.

units.la: 11 Hoc omnes Israelita audiant, & timeant, ne vltra defignentrem[?] tam ne-fandam in medio tui.
units.tr: 11 And all Israel shall hear, and fear, and shall do no more any such wickedness as this is among you.

units.la: Quanquam Moses veræ pietatis & religionis sustentandæ studio doctores falsos pre-cul ab Ecclesia repellendos docet, hocq; ipso damnum satanæ haud paruū dedit: ta-men cum satan ipse pro sua aduersus Deum pertinaci rebellione minime definens,quod hac non successerit,alia aggrediatur via,ac quod publice non audeat hoc ipsum priuatim faciat: Moses etiam hac ipsam ei obstruit viam: quando in præsentia docet clandestinos prædicatores è rep.profligandos. In quo negotio ordinem eundem omnino seruat,quo prius usus est in repellendis ijs,qui doctrinam falsam publice spargerent: nempe, vt primum de persona,tum de dictis & factis,denique de cauendis & profligandis ipsis.
units.tr: Although Moses, out of zeal for sustaining true piety and religion, teaches that false teachers are to be driven far from the Church, and by this very act inflicted no small loss on Satan, yet Satan, by no means giving up his stubborn rebellion against God, when this has not succeeded, attacks by another route, and what he does not dare to do in public he does in private. So Moses also blocks this very path for him, when in the present passage he teaches that secret preachers must be driven out of the commonwealth. In this matter he keeps altogether the same order he followed before in repelling those who spread false doctrine publicly: namely, first concerning the person, then concerning their words and deeds, and finally concerning how they are to be guarded against and driven out.

units.la: De eorum persona. Si te clanculum folicitauerit frater tuus,filius matris tuæ,aut filius tuus,aut filia tua,aut vxor gremij tui,&c. Quibus verbis eos potissimum nominat, quorum o-pera satan in primis ecclesiam inficit, si quid clam agat. Ac primo loco fratrem nominat,& vt ostendat quantum inde fit periculi,subdit, filius matris tuæ: quo docet arctissimâ necessitudinem, qua coniuncti inter se fratres sint ac videantur esse. Vnde fit vt frater fratrem se-ducat facillime quippe qui videatur bene velle consultum. Et hoc periculum pertimescit in euangelioD.cum dicit eum,qui fratres magis,quam ipsum diligat,ipso indignum esse. Quare ne quam fratris hac in re præsertim habeas rationem vide.
units.tr: Concerning their person: If thy brother, the son of thy mother, or thy son, or thy daughter, or the wife of thy bosom, etc. By these words he names especially those through whose work Satan above all infects the Church, when he acts in secret. First he names the brother, and to show how great the danger is, he adds "the son of thy mother": by which he teaches the very close bond by which brothers are joined and seem to be joined. Hence it happens that a brother very easily seduces a brother, since he seems to wish him well. And in the Gospel the Lord fears this danger when he says that one who loves brothers more than him is unworthy of him. Wherefore, lest you show any regard to a brother in this matter, take heed.

units.la: Liberos deinceps nominat,qui cum sint sanguis nostri, & caro nostra quasi alteri ipsi, placet nobis quicquid hi dicunt & faciunt. [illegible, ~12 letters] Vt in corpore nevos,sic in animis errores,quos habent non cernimus.
units.tr: Next he names children, who, since they are our blood and our flesh, are as it were another self, and so we approve whatever these say and do. [illegible, ~12 letters] As we do not see the moles on the body, so we do not see the errors in the minds of our children.

units.la: Vxor & thori & bonorum omnium & vitæ consors est: nec cuiusquam verbis adeo fa-cile flectimur atque vxorum:etenim ceu magnes lapis ad se trahunt.. Adam summa fuit prudentia,quippe qui rerum naturam adeo exploratè cognitam haberet, vt illis conuenientia inderet nomina: sed vxoris verbis falsus & flexus est, vt præceptum Dei conditoris negligeret.Samsonis robur quodnullo Marte vinci potuit,astu muliebri victum atq; oppressum est. Dauidis felicitas & victoriæ nullis exterorum regum copijs turbari potuere: sed amore mulierum infectæ sunt.Solomonis sapientia mulierum illecebris obruta est. Herodias scelesta atque incesta pellex impedimento fuit, quo minus apud Herodem Baptistæ proficeret concionando & consulendo. Sed exemplis refertæ sunt omnes historiæ. Quæ docent ne Syrenum illarum vocibus sic te dementari patiare, vt verum religionis genus deseras. Proximus qui est quasi anima tua, hoc est, amicus intimus. Saepe enim amicitiæ fiunt agnatione firmiores: veluti fuerunt amicorum paria Dauid Ionathas, Pylades & Orestes, Nisus & Eurialus, & complures alij. Et accidit ut amicos & socios defertis parentibus, uxore, liberis, &c. sequamur. Ab his ut in vita ac moribus, sic etiam in religione est periculum. Vere enim Paulus ait, corrumpere bonos mores colloquia praua.
units.tr: A wife is partner of the bed, of all goods and of life; nor are we turned so easily by anyone's words as by those of wives, for they draw us to themselves like a magnet stone. Adam had the greatest prudence, since he knew the nature of things so thoroughly that he gave them fitting names; yet he was deceived and turned by his wife's words, so that he neglected the command of God the Creator. Samson's strength, which no war could conquer, was overcome and crushed by feminine cunning. David's good fortune and victories could not be disturbed by the forces of foreign kings, yet they were undone by love of women. Solomon's wisdom was overwhelmed by the allurements of women. Herodias, the wicked and incestuous concubine, was an obstacle to Baptist's preaching and counsel gaining anything with Herod. But all histories are full of examples. They teach you not to let yourself be driven mad by the voices of those Sirens so that you abandon the true religion. "Your neighbour, who is as your own soul," means your intimate friend. For friendships are often firmer than kinship: examples of such pairs of friends are David and Jonathan, Pylades and Orestes, Nisus and Euryalus, and many others. And it happens that we follow friends and companions, abandoning parents, wife, children, and so on. From these there is danger to life and morals, and also to religion. For truly Paul says, "Evil communications corrupt good manners."

units.la: Atq; sic quidem personas nominat, ut ab his tibi scias esse abstinendum.
units.tr: Thus he names the persons, so that you may know you must keep away from them.

units.la: De eorum studijs sic dicit, Si te clanculum solicitauerit dicens, Eamus & seruiamus Dijs alijs, quos nec tu nouisti, nec patres tui, fuerintque ex Dijs populorum, qui circum vos sunt, siue prope fuerint tecum, siue procul, &c. Quibus ex verbis est perspicuum qua ratione per hos satan decipiat. 1. Clam seu tecte agit. Nam verbum Hebræum significat occulere, celare, & aliquid abscondere: quo spiritus sanctus usus indicat illos clam, & in angulis agitare hæc consilia cum publice non audeant. Quibus susurris nihil est perniciosius. Quemadmodum enim putredo ligna, vlcera vero corpus, sic illi pacem & tranquillitatem publicam rodunt. Proinde Paulus eos remouendos censet, Corrumpunt bonos mores colloquia praua, inquiens. Ac veluti in castris seditiosus nebulo ducem, exercitum, belli causam, omnia patria vituperans ac hostilia vehens laudibus, ni coerceatur, exercitu omnem inficit: sic impurus aliquis nebulo Christum, euangelium, ecclesiam, quæ deniq; Christiana sunt omnia vituperans damnum ecclesiæ dat maximum, ac præstaret hostem profes-sum esse.
units.tr: Concerning their pursuits he speaks thus: If thy brother secretly entice thee, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, which thou hast not known, neither thou nor thy fathers, namely, of the gods of the peoples which are round about you, whether nigh unto thee or far off, etc. From these words it is clear by what method Satan deceives through these people. 1. They act secretly or covertly. For the Hebrew word means to hide, to conceal, and to keep something out of sight; the Holy Spirit uses it to show that these men carry on their plans in secret and in corners, since they do not dare to do so openly. Nothing is more harmful than such whisperings. For as rot eats wood and ulcers eat the body, so they gnaw away public peace and tranquillity. Therefore Paul judges they must be removed: "Evil communications corrupt good manners," he says. And just as in a camp a seditious rascal, disparaging the commander, the army, the cause of the war and the whole fatherland, and spreading hostile talk under the guise of praise, infects the whole army unless he is restrained, so an impure rascal who disparages Christ, the gospel, the Church, and in the end everything that is Christian, does the Church the greatest harm; it would be better to have an open enemy.

units.la: 2 Argumenta habet. Seruiamus Dijs alienis, quos non nosti. En obtendit simplicitatem & ignorantiam. Ut Hieroboam dixit in Bethel potius sacrificandum esse quàm Hierosolymis, ne videlicet adeò longo itinere frustra fatigarentur homines: quasi vero maiores parum prudenter sibi consuluerint, qui in longinquis locis potius quàm in propinquis volu-erint sacrificare. Pharisæi suas traditiones Mosaicis legibus addiderunt, quasi illæ quid facto opus esset non plene traderent. Papistæ suis traditionibus hunc prætextum paratum habent: Ecclesiam apostolicam fuisse rudem & simplicem, ac post autem usu multa cognouisse & constituisse quæ priores ignorassent: tum literis apostolicis non omnia, quæ ad salutem spectant, comprehendi: quæ de causa patrum, conciliorum, synodorum, pontificum, decreta esse necessaria.
units.tr: 2. He offers arguments: Let us serve other gods, whom you have not known. See, he pleads simplicity and ignorance. So Jeroboam said it was better to sacrifice at Bethel than at Jerusalem, so that people would not be wearied in vain by so long a journey; as if our forefathers had consulted their own good unwisely when they preferred to sacrifice in distant places rather than near ones. The Pharisees added their traditions to the Mosaic laws, as if these did not fully hand down what was needed for the matter. The Papists have this pretext ready for their traditions: that the apostolic Church was rude and simple, and afterwards, through experience, learned and established many things which the earlier Church had not known; and that not everything which pertains to salvation is comprised in the apostolic writings. For this reason, they say, the decrees of the Fathers, councils, synods and popes are necessary.

units.la: Dein sunt exempla populorum plærorumque. Num vos soli sapitis? Atque hæc cauenda. Opus exemplis, sed omnium perfectissimum est Christus, quem pater propositit: tum sunt illius imitatores apostoli. Nec sine causa dictum est, per publicam viam ne ieris.
units.tr: Then there are the examples of the many peoples: "Are you alone wise?" These things must be guarded against. Examples are needed, but the most perfect of all is Christ, whom the Father set forth; then the apostles are his imitators. Nor without cause is it said, "Do not walk in the public way."

units.la: De ratione eos cauendi. Ne acquiescas ei, neque audies eum nec ei parcat oculus tuus, neque indulgeas, &c. Quibus verbis docet eum puniendum, atq; ut id obtineat primum suppliciorum formam, tum impedimenta simul atq; causas profert. Ac quoniam impedimenta causis efficientibus obstant, ea ipsa primum omnium remouet.
units.tr: On how they are to be guarded against: Thou shalt not consent unto him, nor hearken unto him, neither shall thine eye pity him, neither shalt thou spare, etc. By these words he teaches that such a man must be punished. To secure this, he first sets out the form of punishment, and then at once names the impediments and the causes. And since impediments stand in the way of the efficient causes, he first of all removes these.

units.la: Impediunt autem pœnas seu iusta iudicia fere hæc duo: socordia videlicet & præposte-ra clementia. Socordiam hoc ipso remouet quod dicit: ne acquiescas, neue audias, ne sis tam mollis ut flectare, nec tam stultus ut audias. Præposteram calumniam arcet ad hunc modum: Ne parcat, inquit, oculus tuus, neue ei indulgeas, neue eum absconda. Crudelior est qui lupo in gregem grassanti parcit, quàm qui lupum ferit ut gregem conseruet saluum.
units.tr: Now two things chiefly hinder punishment or just judgment: namely, carelessness and misplaced clemency. He removes carelessness by this very command: "Do not consent, nor listen; do not be so soft that you are bent, nor so foolish that you hear him." He guards against misplaced clemency in this way: "Let not your eye spare him, do not indulge him, do not conceal him." He is more cruel who spares a wolf rushing into the flock than he who strikes the wolf so as to keep the flock safe.

units.la: Modus is est, quem ab Israelitis seruatum omnes testantur historiæ, ut singuli singulis eum lapidibus obruant. Sed est alius Deut.17.de pœnis locus.
units.tr: The manner is the one which all histories attest was observed by the Israelites, that each man would overwhelm him with stones, one by one. But there is another passage about punishments, Deut. 17.

units.la: Causas autem has refert. 1. Quod sollicitauit ad defectionem à Deo. Magnum scelus, vi-delicet. Quis enim est qui nos maiore amore prosequatur, & pluribus ijsque maximis augeat beneficijs? Unum hic omisisis[?] ceteris commemorat, liberauit, inquiens, ex Ægypto. 2. Exemplum, ut timeant alij Israelitæ & non idem faciant, hic enim finis pœnis omnibus est finis. Propositus. Quod enim impune licet, id eo magis patratur crimen. At ut & Deo suus sit salvus honos, & ut salua sit ecclesia, danda est opera, ut quæ vergunt in Dei ignominiam reprimantur: quæ vero ad promotionem eius gloriæ videntur pertinere, ea quanto maximo potest fieri studio moliamur per Christum Iesum Dominum nostrum. Amen.
units.tr: He gives the causes. 1. Because he has sought to entice you to defection from God. A great crime, certainly. For who is there who pursues us with greater love and enriches us with more and greater benefits? Here he passes over the rest and mentions one: he freed us, he says, out of Egypt. 2. The example: that the other Israelites may fear and not do the same. For this is the purpose set before us by all punishments. A crime is committed all the more readily when it goes unpunished. But so that God's honour may remain safe and the Church may be safe, care must be taken that whatever tends to God's dishonour is suppressed; and whatever seems to pertain to the advancement of his glory, we should labour at with the greatest zeal possible, through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

units.la: 12 Si in aliqua urbium tuarum, quas Dominus Deus tuus dat tibi ut in eis habites, audieris hanc famam.
units.tr: 12 If you hear in one of your cities, which the LORD your God gives you to dwell in, this report:

units.la: 13 Egressi sunt viri filij Belial e medio tui & sollicitarunt cives urbis suae hi-sce verbis, Eamus & serviamus dijs alijs, quos non noveritis.
units.tr: 13 Certain men, sons of Belial, have gone out from among you and have enticed the inhabitants of their city, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, whom you have not known.

units.la: 14 Inquiras, inuestiges, & interroges diligenter, & si verum est, & certum ver-bum illud quod istiusmodi abominatio facta sit in medio tui.
units.tr: 14 Then you shall inquire, search out, and examine diligently; and if it is true and certain that such an abomination has been done among you,

units.la: 15 Omnino feries inhabitatores illius civitatis gladio, & vastato eam gladio, & quicquid in ea est, etiam iumenta eius.
units.tr: 15 you shall surely put the inhabitants of that city to the sword, destroying it utterly with the sword, and everything in it, even its cattle.

units.la: 16 Vniuersa autem spolia eius comportabis in medium fori eius, & succendes urbem igne, & in universum omnia spolia eius Domino Deo tuo, ut sit perpetuo acer-vus, nec readificetur amplius.
units.tr: 16 You shall gather all its spoil into the middle of its open square, and burn the city with fire, with all its spoil, as a whole burnt offering to the LORD your God; and it shall be a heap forever, and shall never be rebuilt.

units.la: 17 Nec hærebit in manu tua quidquam de illo Herem, ut reuertatur Domi-nus à furore iræ suæ, & intimo affectu erga te commoueatur, misereaturq; tui, & mul-tiplicet te, quemadmodum iurauit patribus tuis.
units.tr: 17 Nothing of that accursed thing shall cling to your hand, so that the LORD may turn from the fierceness of his anger, and show you compassion, and have mercy on you, and multiply you, as he swore to your fathers.

units.la: 18 Audies itaque vocem Domini Dei tui, ut custodias omnia præcepta eius, quæ ego præcipio tibi hodie, ut quod rectum est in oculis Domini Dei tui facias.
units.tr: 18 If you obey the voice of the LORD your God, keeping all his commandments which I command you today, doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD your God.

units.la: Ræclare est à Diuo Petro scriptum in i.epist.[?] 5.cap. Satanam aduersarium nostrum ceu leonem rugientem obambulare, & quam deuoret prædam quærere: qua de causa nobis sit vigilandum & hosti tanto eundum obuiam fide & constantia. Id verum esse cum verbis Domini Christi, tum exemplis aliis atq; aliis probari potest. Dominus probat parabolis de zizanijs, & de spiritu septemplici purgatam domum repetente, & cohortationibus multis generis eiusdem alijs: sunt autem exemplo Iob, spiritus Achabum decipiens per pseudo-prophetas, & satan cribare volens apostolos, imo ipsum etiam, qui invictus est, tentans Domini.
units.tr: It is well written by the divine Peter in 1 Peter 5, that Satan, our adversary, prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour; for which reason we must be watchful and resist this enemy with faith and steadfastness. That this is true can be proved both by the words of the Lord Christ and by many other examples. The Lord proves it by the parables of the tares and of the unclean spirit returning with seven others to the cleansed house, and by many other exhortations of the same kind. Examples are Job, the spirit that deceived Ahab through false prophets, and Satan who wanted to sift the apostles, and even the one who tempted the unconquered Lord himself.

units.la: Ex quibus omnibus potest intelligi satanam in eorrumpenda ecclesia esse & fuisse sem-per impigrum: ac si hic non succedat alia rem tentare via. Id ipsum etiam hoc loco Moses di-cit, tria pseudoprophetarum genera commemorans, per quos palàm, clàm, vi publica aggre-diatur ecclesiam.
units.tr: From all these things it can be understood that Satan is and always has been tireless in corrupting the Church, and that if he does not succeed by one way he tries another. Moses says this very thing in this place, when he recounts three kinds of false prophets, through whom he attacks the Church openly, secretly, and by public violence.

units.la: Ac quoniam de duobus dictum est, sequitur ut dicatur etiam de tertio. In quo primum ge-nus ipsum, tum autem iudicij in ipsum exercendi formam tradit.
units.tr: And since two kinds have been spoken of, it follows that the third should also be spoken of. Here he first sets out this kind itself, and then gives the form of judgment to be exercised against it.

units.la: De tertio genere dicit, Si in aliqua urbium tuarum quas Dominus Deus tuus dat tibi, ut in eis habites, audieris hanc famam, &c. Quibus verbis ad perficiendam huius generis descriptio-nem tres potissimum circumstantias affert, locum, personas, factum. Locus est, aliqua urbi-um earum quas divinitus acceperis. In quo quid Deus præcipiat vide. Non iubet in Ægypto nec vspiam alibi reformationem suscipere, sed earum, quæ tuæ sunt, urbium curam habere. Sunt distincta rerum dominia, quorum sua cuiq; curæ sint magistratui: ita ut Spartam quisq; suam ornet, & eos regat in quos habet imperium. Sic in nostros nos intenti simus.
units.tr: Of the third kind he says: If you hear in one of your cities, which the LORD your God gives you to dwell in, this report, etc. In these words, to complete the description of this kind, he gives three chief circumstances: place, persons, and deed. The place is one of those cities which you have received from God. Notice what God commands in this regard. He does not order that reform be undertaken in Egypt or anywhere else, but that care be taken of those cities which are yours. Dominions over things are distinct, and each should have its own cares committed to its magistrate, so that each man adorns his own Sparta and rules those over whom he has authority. So let us be intent on our own affairs.

units.la: Verum observa quod addit, quas Dominus Deus dat tibi, ut meminerint eius, à quo suum acceperunt imperium. Sæpe enim quasi sua ipsorum sint propria, sic abutuntur reges impe-rijs. Paulus autem Dei ministerium vocat magistratum. Deus ostendit Psalm.81. se esse in medio consultantium, ut intelligat quid contra se geratur facillime. Quamobrem ut sis industri us[?] cogita Dei donum esse, tantoq; tibi debere esse charius. Sic præstaret nostram nobis esse Heluetiam[?], quam principes aut populos exteros.
units.tr: But observe what he adds: which the LORD your God gives you, so that they may remember from whom they have received their authority. For rulers often abuse their power as if it were their own property. Paul, however, calls the magistracy God's ministry. In Psalm 81 God shows that he is in the midst of those who take counsel, so that he may most readily understand what is done against him. Therefore, that you may be diligent, consider that the magistracy is God's gift, and that you ought to hold it all the more dear. So it would be better for us to have Switzerland as our own than foreign princes or peoples.

units.la: Personæ,filij Belial: qui quales quàm sint, & ex ethymo & ex Scripturis potest intelligi. Ethymon significat eum, qui non proficiat, ab בלי[?] non & יעל[?] ascendet: id est, qui non augeatur, qui impius fit, propterea, ut Psal.1. dicitur, nec vigeat nec floreat. Exempla habes Iud. 19.1.Reg.1.2.21.25. homines perditis moribus.
units.tr: The persons: sons of Belial. What sort of men these are can be understood both from the etymology and from Scripture. The etymology signifies one who does not profit, from bli [בלי], not, and yaal [יעל], ascend; that is, one who is not increased, who becomes impious; therefore, as it is said in Psalm 1, he neither thrives nor flourishes. You have examples in Judges 19; 1 Kings 1, 2, 21, 25: men of ruined morals.

units.la: En ut eiusmodi pestes Deus odio habeat, atque auersetur.
units.tr: Behold how God hates and turns away from such pests.

units.la: Factum, solicitant cives urbis suae, eamus & serviamus dijs alienis, quos non nosti. Docet, eos astrahere à vero cultu Dei. Idque efficiunt tanto maiore cum incommodo, quanto sunt plures & robustiores. Id vero satan agit, ut quod privatim nequit, id vi publica perficiat. Sic HieroboHieroboam,Iesabel,Nabuchodonozor,Antiochus,Judæorum pontifices, Arriani,papæ,Mahometes,anabaptistæ vi publica blasphemos errores defenderunt. Quod genus coniurationes interdum etiam civilibus in causis existunt authore satana, velut Romæ Catilinaria,bellum rusticum in Germania,& nonnulli tumultus in Heluetia. Quibus ceu instrumentis satan & corpora & animas rapit: ut videas spiritum istum septemplicem,de quo Christus dicit in Euangelio. Res nequaquam contemnendæ,sed quibus mature sit eundum obviam. Qui id facias disceptatum est à multis,& varie. Augustinus primum negavit plectendos esse capite,post usu melius edoctus diversum sensit. Quin é verbo Domini,& exemplo veteris ecclesiæ quid facto opus sit Moses docet.
