First, what is holy is owed to the sanctuary, as a payment due to God; and whatever you give sanctifies your remaining goods, while whatever you keep unjustly defiles your remaining wealth, like Tolosan gold. Second, because God has commanded it, and to pass it over or consign it to forgetfulness is the greatest sin. Let us examine ourselves in this mirror.

units.la: De altero dicit,se hæc minimè contulisse in malos vsus. 1. Non comedi in dolore: id est,e-tiam egens his vsus non sum.Et tamen hic prætextus vulgò quæritur, sed quo iure præsens locus indicat.
units.tr: Of the second he says that he has not put these things to evil uses. 1. I have not eaten in sorrow: that is, even when in need I have not used them for such purposes. And yet this excuse is commonly sought, but the present passage shows by what right it may be claimed.

units.la: 2. Nec sustuli in immundiciam,in res prophanas,turpes,malas.
units.tr: 2. Nor have I taken any of it away in uncleanness, that is, into profane, base or evil things.

units.la: 3. Nec in mortuos,vt funebres pompas,Diuorum aras,statuas,cultum. Quibus iniquum est,& inutile dari quo carent viui,ὀλ/ωθε/ις[?].
units.tr: 3. Nor have I given any of it to the dead, as to funeral pomps, altars of the deified, statues, or worship. It is unjust and useless to give to the dead what the living lack [ὀλ/ωθε/ις].

units.la: Sed audiui vocem Domini,& feci,&c. Ergo malum est in res prophanas eleemosynas stas conuertere.
units.tr: But I have heard the voice of the Lord, and have done, etc. Therefore it is wrong to turn sacred alms to profane uses.

units.la: Iam quoniam hæc impulsu Dei facimus : cum Dauide precemur : cor mundum in me crea Deus,spiritum rectum innoua in visceribus meis.Qui spiritum hunc non habent,ij non sunt Dei.Sed Ezechias eodem spiritu potuit præstare, quod dicit de se , Memento Domine quomodo ambulauerim coram te in veritate,& in corde perfecto:quibus verbis non se, verum Dei in se munera commendat.
units.tr: Now, since we do these things by the impulse of God, let us pray with David: "Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within my bowels." Those who do not have this spirit are not God's. But Hezekiah, by that same spirit, was able to offer what he says of himself: "Remember, O Lord, how I have walked before you in truth and with a perfect heart." In these words he commends not himself but the gifts of God in him.

units.la: Ex hac deinceps conscientiæ bonitate spes animis oboritur minimè dubia,fore vt sua in nobis dona aliquando condignis præmijs sit ornaturus Dominus.Vnde dicitur in altera parte, Aspice nos de habitaculo sancto tuo de cœlis & benedic populum tuum Israel,&c. In quo vide mus quantæ spes sint ijs repositæ, qui secuti præcepta Dei summa fide egenis opem ferunt: aspicit illos Deus:benedicit illis Deus: largitur omnia bona promissa.Itaq; spem roboramus beneficentia.Vt sementem feceris,ita & metes.Matth.25.Iob,Tobias,patriarchæ suis eleemo synis & hospitalitate diuitias auxere non minuere suas.
units.tr: From this goodness of conscience there arises in our minds a hope that is by no means doubtful: that the Lord will at some time adorn his gifts in us with fitting rewards. Hence it is said in the other part: Look down upon us from your holy habitation in heaven, and bless your people Israel, etc. In this we see how great are the hopes laid up for those who, following the precepts of God, bring help to the needy with the highest faith: God looks upon them, God blesses them, God grants all the good things promised. And so we strengthen our hope by beneficence. "As you have sown, so shall you also reap" (Matth. 25.). Job and Tobias, the patriarchs, by their alms and hospitality increased their riches; they did not diminish them.

units.la: Qua de causa,nempe propter eam quæ summi boni causa est, hominis cum Deo coniun ctionis & amicitiæ.Ea Deum facit nostrum : quod scire fideliū est proprium.Omnibus enim etiam malis spiritibus constat esse Deum:at suum esse non constat nisi fidelibus.
units.tr: For this reason, namely because of that which is the cause of the highest good, the union and friendship of man with God, this beneficence makes God ours, which is the proper knowledge of the faithful. For it is agreed by all, even evil spirits, that God exists, but that he is ours is agreed only by the faithful.

units.la: Rursus eadem nos populum Dei facit:quod agnoscere est ipsum etiam fidelium. Veluti Rom.8.docet apostolus spiritum arrabonem testem esse nostræ adoptionis.
units.tr: Again, the same beneficence makes us the people of God, which is to acknowledge even the faithful themselves. As the apostle teaches in Rom. 8., the Spirit is the pledge and witness of our adoption.

units.la: Medium quo coniungimur est ipsum verbum Domini, cuius qui studiosi sunt ad simili-tudinem Dei subinde magis ac magis confirmantur. Ac quoniam simile simili gaudet & pa-res cum paribus facillimè congregantur : quemadmodum in omni amicitia similitudo mo-rum & consensus consiliorum & voluntatum potissimum sociat ac iungit homines:sic imita-tione Dei & studio præceptorum eius fit,vt cum illo in arctius societatis vinculum coeamus.' Idipsum hic Moses dicit alludens ad verba fœderis,Gen.17.Exod.20.
units.tr: The means by which we are joined is the very Word of the Lord, and those who are zealous for it are continually more and more strengthened into the likeness of God. And since like delights in like, and equals most easily gather with equals, just as in every friendship similarity of manners and agreement of counsels and wills chiefly joins and unites men, so by imitating God and by zeal for his precepts it comes about that we come together with him into a closer bond of fellowship. Moses says this very thing here, alluding to the words of the covenant (Gen. 17.; Exod. 20.).

units.la: Ex quibus intelligitur oportere nos esse Deo gratos , gratamq; voluntatem eam officijs in Leuitas,pauperes & viduas quasi in Deum ipsum testari.Ei sit honos in secula,Amen.
units.tr: From these things it is understood that we ought to be pleasing to God, and to bear witness to that pleasing will, through duties toward the Levites, the poor and the widows, as if toward God himself. To him be honour for ever, Amen.

units.la: CAPVT XXVII. SERMO LXVI.
units.tr: CHAPTER 27. SERMON 66.

units.la: Præcepit Moses & seniores Israel populo,dicentes: Custodite omnia præcepta, quæ ego præcipio vobis hodie.
units.tr: Moses and the elders of Israel charged the people, saying: Keep all the commandments which I command you this day.

units.la: 2 Hoc vero fiet cum traieceritis Iordanem,(veneritisq; in terram,quam Dominus Deus tuus dat tibi,erige lapides magnos,& obduc eos calce.
units.tr: 2 And this shall be done when you have passed over the Jordan (and have come into the land which the Lord your God gives you), you shall set up great stones and plaster them with lime.

units.la: 3 Scribeq; super eos omnia verba legis huius quando transieris, eò quod veneris in terram,quam Dominus Deus tuus dat tibi , terram fluentem lacte & melle,sicut loquutus est Dominus Deus patrum tuorum tibi.
units.tr: 3 And you shall write upon them all the words of this law when you have passed over, because you have come into the land which the Lord your God gives you, a land flowing with milk and honey, as the Lord the God of your fathers has spoken to you.

units.la: 4 Quando itaq; Iordanem traieceritis,erigetis lapides istos,quos ego hodie vobis præcipio in monte Ebal,& obduretis eos calce.
units.tr: 4 When therefore you have passed over the Jordan, you shall set up these stones, which I command you this day, on Mount Ebal, and you shall plaster them with lime.

units.la: 5 Ædificabis quoque ibi aram Domino Deo tuo,aram de lapidibus,super quos ferrum non leuabis.
units.tr: 5 There you shall also build an altar to the Lord your God, an altar of stones, over which you shall not lift up iron.

units.la: 6 De lapidibus integris ædificabis aram Domini Dei tui, & sacrificabis super eam holocaustum Domino Deo tuo.
units.tr: 6 You shall build the altar of the Lord your God of whole stones, and you shall offer upon it a burnt offering to the Lord your God.

units.la: 7 Sacrificabis quoq; pacifica sacrificia, et comedes ibi, lætaberisq; coram Domino Deo tuo.
units.tr: 7 You shall also offer peace offerings, and eat there, and you shall rejoice before the Lord your God.

units.la: 8 Et scribes super lapides omnia verba legis huius, idq; luculenter & clarè.
units.tr: 8 And you shall write upon the stones all the words of this law, and that plainly and clearly.

units.la: 9 Loquutusq; est Moses, & sacerdotes Leuitici generis ad universum Israelem in hunc modum: Israel ausculta & audi: Hodie factus es populus Domini Dei tui.
units.tr: 9 And Moses and the priests of the Levitical race spoke to all Israel in this manner: Israel, hearken and listen: this day you have become the people of the Lord your God.

units.la: 10 Audies igitur vocem Domini Dei tui, & facies præcepta eius, atq; statuta eius, quæ ego præcipio tibi hodie.
units.tr: 10 You shall therefore hear the voice of the Lord your God, and do his commandments and his statutes, which I command you this day.

units.la: Vemadmodum diuinus Moses superiore cap. exercitia duo præscribit, quibus omnium Dei in nos beneficiorum admoniti Deo grati simus, & nostram in illum fidem subinde magis ac magis roboremus: sic illo 27. cap. alium quendam ritum affert, quo populum in assiduo diuinarum legum vsu contineat. Qui ritus hic quidem describitur, sed exemplo populi Iof. 8. magis illustratur. Est autem summa ac caput rei, vt populus in terram sanctam ingressus nec præsentis fortunæ suauitate delinitus atq; fractus, nec oblitus superioris miseriæ, remittat aliquid de diuinarum legum studio, lapidibus erectis aram struat, in qua Deo dator i sacrificet: verba legis inscribat, diuini fœderis explicationem audiat: populus ipse duabus partibus distributus, hinc benedictiones inde maledictiones referat. Ex quo perspicuum est ritum illum quinq; partibus constare, quæ singulæ mentem nostram ad Dei cultus atque pietatis studium queant excitare: vt ara, sacrificijs, scriptione legum, verbi diuini doctrina atque ministerio: populi consensu atq; suffragijs.
units.tr: As the divine Moses in the previous chapter prescribed two exercises by which, being reminded of all God's benefits toward us, we may be grateful to God and from time to time strengthen our faith in him more and more, so in this 27th chapter he sets out another rite, by which he keeps the people in constant use of the divine laws. This rite is indeed described here, but it is further illustrated by the example of the people in Joshua 8. The sum and heart of the matter is this: when the people has entered the holy land, it must neither be softened and broken by the sweetness of present fortune, nor forget its former misery, and it must not relax anything of its zeal for the divine laws. Let it build an altar of erected stones, on which it sacrifices to the giver of God; let it inscribe the words of the law; let it hear the explanation of the divine covenant; and let the people itself, divided into two parts, recite here the blessings and there the curses. From this it is plain that the rite consists of five parts, each of which can stir our minds to the worship of God and the pursuit of piety: (1) the altar; (2) the sacrifices; (3) the writing of the laws; (4) the teaching and ministry of the divine word; (5) the consent and votes of the people.

units.la: Vnde caput ipsum duabus partibus est distributum: quarum priore cerimoniæ illæ singulatim singulæ referuntur, posteriore populi suffragia continentur.
units.tr: Hence the chapter itself is divided into two parts: in the first, those ceremonies are recounted one by one; in the second, the votes of the people are contained.

units.la: Et illarum cerimoniarum commemorationé ab officio exorsus ordine, quo positæ sunt, prosequitur. Igitur ab officio, ceu causa ad vsum huius ritus impellente, descriptionem illam ad hunc modum auspicatur: Custodite (inquit) omnia præcepta quæ ego præcipio vobis hodie, cū Iordanem, &c. Id est, cum sitis in Dei fœdus asciti, eaq; fœderis capita Dei mandato ego nunc commemorem: certè cum hæc ipsa vobis erunt seruanda, tum quæcunq; Deus ad id studiū submi-nistrat adiumenta diligenter vsurpanda: nec erit existimandum hic quicquam superua cuum præcipi: verum quod diuinitus præcipitur id esse, quia diuinum sit mandatum & quia salutarium rerum studium excitet ac roboret, obseruandum.
units.tr: And having begun the recital of those ceremonies with the duty, he follows them in the order in which they are set down. So, beginning with the duty as the cause that impels us to the use of this rite, he opens the description in this way: Keep (he says) all the commandments which I command you this day, when you pass over the Jordan, etc. That is: since you have been taken into the covenant of God, and I now recall by God's command the heads of that covenant, certainly these very things must be kept by you, and whatever aids God supplies for that zeal must be diligently used. Nor should it be thought that anything superfluous is commanded here; rather, whatever is commanded divinely must be observed, because it is a divine command and because it stirs up and strengthens the pursuit of saving things.

units.la: Atq; hoc quidem de omni diuinarum præceptionum genere statuendum est. Præcipit, Ego sum is qui te Ægypto eduxi Deus: non habebis alienos coram me deos. Perspicuum hoc & clarum præceptum est, sed ratione & sententia natura ab eo ad creaturarum cultum & fiduciam retrahimur, opinati Deum etiam in suis creaturis honorari posse. Qua opinione & gentilis illa πολυθεία, & Christianis hominibus hucusq; vsurpatus Diuorum cultus promanarunt. Dixit, ne quam earum quæ in cœlo, terra, aquis sunt rerum imaginem vel faciamus, vel colamus vel adoremus. Nobis autem visum est bonum statuis, tanquam hominum popularium libris vti: & inde statuarum atq; imaginum vsus atq; cultus exortus est. Quamobrem optimum est quod Moses dicit omissis placitis humanis præcepta Dei custodire.
units.tr: And this must be laid down of every kind of divine precept. He commands: "I am the Lord who brought you out of Egypt: you shall have no other gods before me." This precept is plain and clear, but by a certain reasoning and opinion of nature we are drawn away from it to the worship and trust of creatures, supposing that God can also be honoured in his creatures. From this opinion both that pagan polytheism and the worship of the saints, which has been practised by Christian men up to now, have sprung. He said: "You shall not make or worship or adore any image of those things that are in heaven, earth or waters." But men thought it good to use statues as books for the common people; and from this arose the use and worship of statues and images. Therefore what Moses says is best: setting aside human opinions, keep the precepts of God.

units.la: Sed & ritus ad diuinarum legum studium excitantes quales quales humanæ rationi videantur, studiose diligenter q; seruandi sunt: vt circuncisio, pascha, sacrificia, purgationes populo veteri: vt nobis baptismus, cæna Domini, preces, verbi diuini prædicatio. Hæc enim ideo data sunt vt nostram in Deum fidem excitent, acuant, roborent.
units.tr: But also the rites which stir up zeal for the divine laws, however they may seem to human reason, must be kept carefully and diligently: such as circumcision, the Passover, sacrifices and purifications for the old people; and for us baptism, the Lord's Supper, prayers and the preaching of the divine word. For these were given so that they might stir up, sharpen and strengthen our faith in God.

units.la: Quare tenenda hæc est quasi regula: Quicquid præcipit Dominus seruandum esse. Eam Moses sæpe & iterum inculcat dicens, Neq; dextrorsum neq; sinistrorsum à verbo Dei discedendum. Et Christus de matrimonio differens omnem eam causam ad primæuum mandatū Patris exigit. Paulus de eucharistia dicens: Quod audiui à Domino id docui vos: idem de matrimonio quid facto opus sit præscribens, Non inquit, ego præcipio, sed Dominus. Sic Verbi ministerium dicit esse diuinarum & cœlestium rerum quæsturam. Eodem modo ritum hunc propterea seruandum Moses dicit, quod omnia Dei præcepta qualiacunque sint custodienda.
units.tr: Wherefore this must be held as a kind of rule: whatever the Lord commands must be kept. Moses often repeats this, saying: "Do not turn aside from the word of God, either to the right or to the left." And Christ, discussing marriage, refers every such matter back to the first command of the Father. Paul, speaking of the Eucharist, says: "What I received from the Lord, that I delivered to you"; and in prescribing what must be done about marriage, he says: "Not I, but the Lord, commands." So he calls the ministry of the Word the stewardship of divine and heavenly things. In the same way Moses says that this rite must be kept, because all the precepts of God, of whatever kind, must be kept.

units.la: Cærimonias autem omnes ex Iof. 8. cap. & Exod. 20. plenius cognoscemus: illic enim quasi depictæ carni possunt.
units.tr: Now we shall know all the ceremonies more fully from Joshua 8 and Exodus 20: for there they can be seen as if painted from life.

units.la: De ara fi locum Exodi conferas huc,tres cerimoniæ statuuntur:ut impoliti magni lapi-des erigantur: ut ara ex integris & nullo ferro laboratis lapidibus efficiatur: ut nulli fiant ad aram gradus,ne detegantur pudendæ partes corporis ascendentibus.
units.tr: If you compare the passage of Exodus here about the altar, three ceremonies are laid down: that unhewn great stones be set up; that the altar be made of whole stones not worked by any iron; and that no steps be made to the altar, lest the private parts of those ascending be uncovered.

units.la: Hæc omnia quoniam Christum atque eius fideles repræsentant, illo dato cessant:& nobis iam consideranda sunt quæ latent in his mysteria. Magni lapides, quos non vult arte humana fabrefieri,sunt fideles,quos verbo Dei potius parari, quàm humanis traditionibus angulari summo lapidi vultaccommodari.De qua structura 1.Pet.2.dicit.
units.tr: Since all these things represent Christ and his faithful, they cease when he has been given; and we must now consider the mysteries hidden in them. The great stones, which he does not want fashioned by human art, are the faithful, who are prepared by the word of God rather than by human traditions, and are fitted to the chief cornerstone. Of this building 1 Peter 2 speaks.

units.la: Ara Christus est sine manibus sciissus Dan. 2. Nulla ars humana adhibita : non est ei spe-cies; nec decor Esa.53;Ferrum non est hic adhibendum,ubi numen est placandum precibus, ut in Solomonis templo non auditus est ferri malleive strepitus. Ibi sacrificandum in hac ara,quam Dominus elegit,non in Divis,Dijs,&c.Sicut necIsraelitis licuit alibi,quàm in loco diuinitus constituto sacrificare.
units.tr: The altar is Christ, cut without hands, Daniel 2. No human art is applied: he has no beauty, nor comeliness, Isaiah 53. Iron is not to be applied here, where the deity is to be appeased by prayers; just as in Solomon's temple no sound of iron or hammer was heard. Here one must sacrifice on this altar, which the Lord has chosen, not on the altars of the gods, etc., just as the Israelites were not permitted to sacrifice elsewhere than in the place divinely appointed.

units.la: Gradus ideo voluit esse nullos ut ne pudenda ascendentes nudarent.Egregiè sanè repri-mit spiritus ambitiosos , quos si sequamur in altum quicquid est humanæ inscitiæ[?], malitiæ, miseriæ,id totum proditur.Humilia Deus respicit Psalthe teste. Humiles spiritu seruabit, ut ait Propheta. Humilitas enim multa tegit quæ superbia reuelat. Et qui scrutator est maiesta-tis opprimetur à gloria.
units.tr: He willed there to be no steps, so that those ascending might not expose their nakedness. This plainly restrains ambitious spirits; if we follow them on high, whatever there is of human ignorance, malice and misery is all laid bare. God regards the lowly, as the Psalm bears witness; he will preserve the humble in spirit, as the Prophet says. For humility covers many things which pride reveals; and whoever is a searcher of majesty will be overwhelmed by glory.

units.la: De sacrificijs,Holocaustum, & pacifica sacrificia postulat. Holocaustum, ex præcipuis sa-crificijs est:Hebræis ab ascendendo Græcis à consumendo dicitur. Usi illo Israelitæ in gra-uissimis periculis:ut Noha,Israelitæ à Beniamitis strati,Samuel à Philistijs territo populo.
units.tr: He calls for the sacrifices, the burnt offering, and the peace offerings. The burnt offering is among the chief sacrifices: it is called by the Hebrews from ascending, by the Greeks from consuming. The Israelites used it in the most serious dangers: as Noah did; as the Israelites did when beaten by the Benjamites; as Samuel did when the people was terrified by the Philistines.

units.la: Illud nobis est euangelium,Rom.15. Sum minister Christi in gentes,sacrificans euange-lium Dei,ut fiat oblatio gentium acceptabilis,sanctificata per spiritum sanctum. Rom.12.Prę beatis corpora vestra,&c.
units.tr: That is for us the gospel, Romans 15: "I am a minister of Christ to the Gentiles, sacrificing the gospel of God, that the offering of the Gentiles may be acceptable, sanctified by the Holy Spirit." Romans 12: "I beseech you, present your bodies," etc.

units.la: Dein postulat sacrificia pacifica,quorum duo sunt genera. Vnum eius quod thoda seu confessionis est,Græcè εὐχαριστίας[?],alterum vedebo[?] votum.De quo genere Psalm.49.Non ac-cipiam de domo tua vitulos,neque de gregibus tuis hircos : paulo post, Immola Deo sacrificium laudis & redde altissimo vota tua. Quare in Christo,ceu ara Deo placita,laudes Dei immolabimus.
units.tr: Next he calls for peace offerings, of which there are two kinds. One is that which is a thank offering or of confession, Greek [εὐχαριστίας] (eucharistias); the other is a vow. Of this kind Psalm 49: "I will not take calves from your house, nor goats from your flocks"; and a little later: "Offer to God the sacrifice of praise, and pay your vows to the Most High." Therefore in Christ, as the altar acceptable to God, we shall offer up the praises of God.

units.la: De scriptione.Et scribes super lapides omnia verba legis huius,idq; luculenter & clare. Ut olim lapidibus,sic iam nobis verba legis inscripta sint necesse est. Quod Esaias & Ioel per spiritum sanctum fore prædixere.Rom.1.Ius naturæ est inscriptum cordibus.
units.tr: On the writing. And you shall write upon the stones all the words of this law, and that plainly and clearly. As once the words were written on stones, so now they must be inscribed on us. Isaiah and Joel foretold that this would happen through the Holy Spirit. Rom. 1. The law of nature is written on hearts.

units.la: De verbi ministerio, Moses & Leuitæ dicunt,audi Israel,Hodie factus es populus Domini, &c. Ergo verbi ministerio quid hæc sibi velint monstratur.
units.tr: On the ministry of the Word: Moses and the Levites say, Hear, O Israel, this day you have become the people of the Lord, etc. Here, then, is shown what these words mean for the ministry of the Word.

units.la: Causa finalis hoc ritu potissimum respiciẽda est, ut iniiti fœderis admoneamur. Idvt saluti fit per Iesum Christum Deus faxit.Amen.
units.tr: The final cause of this rite should be considered above all, namely that we may be reminded of the covenant we have entered. May God grant that this come about for our salvation through Jesus Christ. Amen.

units.la: SERMO LXVII.
units.tr: Sermon 67

units.la: 11 Præcepit, Moses populo illo die, dicens,
units.tr: 11 And Moses charged the people the same day, saying,

units.la: 12 Hi stabunt ad benedicendum populo super montem Garizim cum transferi-tis Iordanem, Simeon, Levi, Iebuda, Isachar, Iofeph, & Beniamin.
units.tr: 12 These shall stand upon mount Gerizim to bless the people, when ye are come over Jordan: Simeon, and Levi, and Judah, and Issachar, and Joseph, and Benjamin.

units.la: 13 Et isti stabunt ad execrandum in monte Ebal, Ruben, Gad, Aser, Zebu-lon, Dan, & Nephtali.
units.tr: 13 And these shall stand upon mount Ebal to curse; Reuben, Gad, and Asher, and Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.

units.la: 14 Levitæ quoq; conceptū verbis dicent ad cunctos Israelitas sublata voce.
units.tr: 14 And the Levites shall speak, and say unto all the men of Israel with a loud voice,

units.la: 15 Execratus vir ille quicunq; fecerit sculptile aut fusile simulachrum, abominatione Domini, opus manuum artificis, posuerit[?] illud in abscondito. Et respondebunt[?] universi de populo, & dicent, Amen.
units.tr: 15 Cursed be the man that maketh any graven or molten image, an abomination unto the LORD, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and putteth it in a secret place. And all the people shall answer and say, Amen.

units.la: 16 Execratus est qui maledicit patri suo aut matri suæ, & dicet omnis populus Amen.
units.tr: 16 Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother. And all the people shall say, Amen.

units.la: 17 Execratus qui mouet limitem proximi sui, & dicet omnis populus, Amen.
units.tr: 17 Cursed be he that removeth his neighbour's landmark. And all the people shall say, Amen.

units.la: 18 Execratus qui cæcum errare aut impingere facit in itinere, & dicet univer-sus populus, Amen.
units.tr: 18 Cursed be he that maketh the blind to wander out of the way. And all the people shall say, Amen.

units.la: 19 Execratus qui declinare facit iudicium peregrini,pupilli,& viduæ,& dicet vniuersus populus Amen.
units.tr: 19 Cursed be he that perverteth the judgment of the stranger, fatherless, and widow. And all the people shall say, Amen.

units.la: 20 Execratus qui dormit cum vxore patris sui, quoniam retegit alam patris sui,& dicet omnis populus Amen.
units.tr: 20 Cursed be he that lieth with his father's wife; because he uncovereth his father's skirt. And all the people shall say, Amen.

units.la: 21 Execratus qui cubat cum vllo iumento,& dicet omnis populus Amen.
units.tr: 21 Cursed be he that lieth with any manner of beast. And all the people shall say, Amen.

units.la: 22 Execratus qui cocumbit cum sorore sua, filia patris sui, aut filia matris sua, & dicet vniuersus populus Amen.
units.tr: 22 Cursed be he that lieth with his sister, the daughter of his father, or the daughter of his mother. And all the people shall say, Amen.

units.la: 23 Execratus qui dormit cum socru sua,& dicet vniuersus populus Amen.
units.tr: 23 Cursed be he that lieth with his mother in law. And all the people shall say, Amen.

units.la: 24 Execratus qui proximum suum clam percutit,et dicet omnis populus Amen.
units.tr: 24 Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly. And all the people shall say, Amen.

units.la: 25 Execratus qui accipit munus,vt percutiat animam sanguinis innocentis,& dicet vniuersus populus Amen.
units.tr: 25 Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person. And all the people shall say, Amen.

units.la: 26 Execratus qui non perfectè præstat verba huius legis vt faciat ea,& dicet vniuersus populus,Amen.
units.tr: 26 Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them. And all the people shall say, Amen.

units.la: IN numerum earum rerum, quibus homines & vt leges diuinas accipiant, incitantur: & vt eas seruent retinentur: Diuus Moses hoc 27.Cap.quendam ritum externum etiam refert, quo populus credentium in tantum diuinæ legis amorem deducatur, vt eam & ratam habeat atq; approbet, & sibi in primis obseruandam suscipiat seq; obstringat. Is ritus quemadmodum quidem seruari debeat cum hic tum supra 11.capite: quemadmodum autem seruatus sit Iof.8.describitur.
units.tr: Among the things by which men are moved to receive the divine laws and are held to keep them, blessed Moses, in chapter 27, also relates a certain external rite, by which the people of believers is brought to such love of the divine law that they hold it valid and approve it, and take it up as the first thing to be observed and bind themselves to it. How this rite ought to be kept is shown both here and above in chapter 11; how it was in fact kept is described in Joshua 8.

units.la: Conueniebat in vnum locum omnis populus, in quo positi lapides, & extructa ara: tum duabus turmis populus distributus à Garizim & ab Hebal stabat: in medio cum arca Leuitæ versus Garizim benedictiones, versus Hebal maledictiones referebant, quibus populus A-men acclamabat. Quo ritu Deus illorum animos commouere voluit, vti leges antea abs se latas approbarent, atque etiam in earum studio permanerent.
units.tr: The whole people gathered into one place, where stones were set up and an altar built. Then the people, divided into two companies, stood, one by Gerizim and the other by Ebal. In the middle, the Levites with the ark pronounced the blessings toward Gerizim and the curses toward Ebal, and the people shouted Amen. By this rite God wished to stir their minds, so that they would approve the laws previously given by him and also persevere in zeal for them.

units.la: In quo non necesse est nos leges iam antea expositas pluribus verbis explicare: sed præstat ad similia studia ritus huius altiore consideratione excitari. Quod fiet si locum, personas, ritum ipsum suo pondere metiamur.
units.tr: In this matter it is not necessary for us to explain at length the laws already set out; it is better to be roused to similar zeal by a closer consideration of this rite. This will happen if we weigh the place, the persons, and the rite itself by its proper weight.

units.la: Locum si consideres sunt duo montes propè Sichem Garizim in Austrum Ebal in Se-ptentrionem ijs, qui ortum respiciunt. Hi modica valle seiunctiq; separatiq; sunt, vt voces utrinque audiri possent. Celebris locus hic locus est. Nam Abraham annos 75. natus cum Loth fratris sui filio, cum vxore & bonis omnibus in Canaan veniens vsque Sichem, aram ibi extruxit & huius terræ promissionem accepit, Gen. 12. Eodem Iacob veniens aram ibidem extruxit, & vt ait Scriptura, tortem[?] Israelis inuocauit, Gen.33. Eodem loco Iacobi filia vitiata, & sacramentum prophanatum est, Gen.seq.ca. Fuit istic etiam templum extructum fortasse in huius rei memoriam: inde etiam aliud Hierosolymitani illius æmulum, quod sub Antiocho Iouis Olympio sacrum fuit, Christi tempore famosum, Ioan.4.
units.tr: As to the place: there are two mountains near Shechem, Gerizim to the south and Ebal to the north, as seen by those facing the east. They are separated and divided by a moderate valley, so that voices could be heard from either side. This place is famous. For Abraham, when he was seventy-five years old, came with his nephew Lot, with his wife and all his goods, into Canaan as far as Shechem, built an altar there and received the promise of this land (Gen. 12). There too Jacob, coming, built an altar, and, as Scripture says, invoked the God of Israel (Gen. 33). In the same place Jacob's daughter was defiled and the covenant sign profaned (Gen. 34). A temple was also built there, perhaps in memory of this matter; from there also came the rival of the Jerusalem temple, which under Antiochus was sacred to Jupiter Olympius, and which was notorious in Christ's time (John 4).

units.la: Id documento est quantopere fit enitendum; vt quibus in locis irritamenta bonorum Deus collocauit, in ijs purum putum bonum conseruemus. Insidiatur enim satan & locis & temporibus & hominibus, vt apostolos, quos sibi Dominus paucos delegerat ad plantandū ac propagandum euangelium, ipse cribrare conatus fuerat, ac Petrum vt laberetur, discipulos reliquos vt fugerent ac desererent Dominum, Iudam vt prorsus degeneraret seq; iret per perditum effecit. Sacros solennesq; dies, quos Deus rerum diuinarum contemplationi destinauit, ille in ocium turpe, luxum & crapulam vertit. Sic templa, scholas, vt Hierosolymam, &c. à pijs vsibus, quibus ea Deus consecrarat, aut ad res prophanas atq; malas aut ad superstitionem & idololatriam transfert. Summa, quocunque loco semen bonum Deus iacit, ille zizania seminat: quocunque tempore nobis benefacere voluerit Dominus, hoc ille nos conatur perdere: quæcunq; bona opera nos moliti fuerimus, ea ille quocunq; potest modo depravat, vt fit in precibus, eleemosynis.
units.tr: This shows how greatly we must strive to keep pure and good in those places where God has set the incentives to good things. For Satan lies in wait by places, times and men. He tried to sift the apostles, whom the Lord had chosen as few to plant and spread the gospel; he worked to make Peter fall, the rest flee and desert the Lord, and Judas degenerate utterly and go to perdition. The sacred and solemn days which God set aside for the contemplation of divine things, he turned into shameful idleness, luxury and drunkenness. So he turns churches and schools, like Jerusalem, away from the holy uses for which God consecrated them, to profane and wicked purposes or to superstition and idolatry. In sum, wherever God sows good seed, he sows tares; at whatever time the Lord wishes to do us good, he tries to ruin us by that time; whatever good works we undertake, he corrupts in whatever way he can, as happens in prayers and almsgiving.

units.la: Personæ, quibus hoc mandatur, duæ sunt populi turmæ, & Leuitæ inter has medij. Sex tribus hæ, Simeon, Leui, Iuda, Ifachar, Ioseph, Beniamin, Iacobo ex Lea & Rahele nati filij in Garizim ad bene precandum constituti.
units.tr: The persons to whom this is commanded are two companies of the people, with the Levites standing between them. The six tribes, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin, sons of Jacob born of Leah and Rachel, are appointed on Gerizim to pronounce blessing.

units.la: Sex tribus illæ, Ruben, Gad, Azer, Zabulon, Dan, Naphtali ex ancillis nati filij in Ebal ad maledicendum constituuntur. Inter has turmas ambas medij Leuitæ cum arca promulgant huc quidem maledictiones transgressoribus irrogatas, illuc vero benedictiones pijs destinatas.
units.tr: Those six tribes, Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali, sons born of the handmaids, are appointed on Ebal to pronounce curses. Between these two companies the Levites with the ark proclaim, on the one side, the curses laid upon transgressors, and on the other, the blessings reserved for the godly.

units.la: Quæ res non caret mysterijs. Nam ingenuis matribus editi quos repræsentant & typis & scripturæ testimonijs indicatur. Isaac enim ex Sara natus quoniam is est, ex quo semen promissum deduci voluit Dominus: typus est eorum, qui sunt ingenui Dei filij, quique amore Dei potius recta sequuntur studia, quàm metu pœnæ. Et hos dicit apostolus synceros esse Dei filios, qui spiritum adoptionis vitæ suæ ducem sequantur.
units.tr: This arrangement is not without mysteries. For the sons born of free mothers, whom the one tribe represents, and the sons born of handmaids, whom the other represents, are indicated both by types and by testimonies of Scripture. Isaac, born of Sarah, since it was through him that the Lord willed the promised seed to be traced, is a type of those who are the free sons of God, and who follow what is right out of love for God rather than fear of punishment. The apostle says these are the true sons of God, who follow the Spirit of adoption as the guide of their lives.

units.la: Hi quoniam Christi fide nituntur, atq; etiam freti faciunt omnia, rectè sanè ad benedicendum depurantur.
units.tr: Since these rest on faith in Christ, and also, relying on him, do all things, they are rightly set apart for blessing.

units.la: Ex ancillis nati matribus seruilia ingenia referunt eorum, qui tantum mali metu non peccant:quos etiam Ismael repræsentat. Oderunt peccare boni virtutis amore: oderunt peccare mali formidine pœnæ.
units.tr: Those born of handmaids, whose slavish dispositions, by their servile mothers, reflect those who refrain from sin only through fear of evil; Ishmael also represents them. Good men hate sin from love of virtue; evil men hate sin from dread of punishment.

units.la: Ruben primogenitus ob peccatum seruilibus illis annumeratur fortasse.
units.tr: Reuben, the firstborn, is perhaps reckoned among those servile sons because of his sin.

units.la: Leuitæ verò, quoniam sunt inter vtrosq; medij summi Dei prædicones, exemplo suo do-cent:ecclesiæ ministrorum hoc interesse, vt sua cuiq; seruanti & transgredienti legem Domini prædicent supplicia & præmia: quid maneat bonos, quid item malos.
units.tr: The Levites, however, since they stand between both as the chief heralds of God, teach by their example that it is the task of the ministers of the church to proclaim to each person, whether keeping or transgressing the law of the Lord, the punishments and rewards: what awaits the good, and likewise what awaits the wicked.

units.la: Iam ipsa benedictionum atque maledictionum promulgatio sic nobis est ponderanda, vt primum eius ipsius capita singula, tum quas ex his percipiamus vtilitates ponderemus.
units.tr: Now the very proclamation of blessings and curses must be weighed in such a way that we consider first each of its separate heads, and then the advantages we gain from them.

units.la: Anathemata illa sunt numero duodecim: quorum vndecim singula peccatum suum habent quod deuoueant: vltimum priora suo quasi ambitu comprehendat. Et hæc omnia sunt ex decem præceptis sumpta.
units.tr: Those curses are twelve in number. Eleven of them each have their own sin which they condemn; the last takes in, as it were in one circuit, the earlier ones. And all of them are taken from the Ten Commandments.

units.la: Primum, Execratus vir ille qui fecerit sculptile, &c. En tibi quod genus idololatriæ vetet, nempe quod animo quisq; suo sibi fingit, ac facit: an illa externa potius simulachra. Sunt qui Mammona, & alia huius generis corde comprehensa atq; erecta simulachra reprehendant, & recte: sed & illa idola Deus vetat, quæ non sunt solum animorum figmenta, verum etiam manuum, vt hic dicitur, opera. Quid igitur illi ganniunt libros laicorum? quid ἀδιάφορα[?]? Dicit hic, maledictum, qui faciat idola, & dicat omnis populus, Amen: cur ergo negant papa, & qui illius ad ollas respiciunt?
units.tr: First, Cursed be the man that maketh any graven image, etc. Here you have what kind of idolatry is forbidden: namely, that which each person fashions and makes for himself in his mind, or rather those external images. There are those who rebuke Mammon and other images of this kind, set up and erected in the heart, and rightly so; but God also forbids those idols which are not merely figments of the mind, but also, as is said here, the work of the hands. Why, then, do they quibble about the books of the laity? And what of adiaphora [ἀδιάφορα]? Here it says: cursed is he who makes idols, and all the people shall say, Amen. Why, then, do the Pope and those who look to his pots deny it?

units.la: Secundum, Execratus qui maledicit patri suo, &c. Pertinet hoc ad primum præceptum secundæ tabulæ, quo nobis mandatur vt parentes, magistros, magistratus, senes colamus, consolemur, foueamus. Per parentes enim hanc ipsam, qua fruimur vitam: per magistros hanc virtutibus & pietate decoratam, qua bene est nobis, vitam: per magistratus hanc pacatam & tranquillam quam, qua bonis datis quiete & suauiter perfruimur, Deus dedit. His qui ingratus sit execratur.
units.tr: Second, Cursed is he who curses his father, etc. This pertains to the first precept of the second table, by which we are commanded to honour, console and cherish parents, teachers, magistrates and the aged. For through parents God gave us this very life that we enjoy; through teachers, this life adorned with virtue and piety, in which it goes well with us; through magistrates, this life kept peaceful and tranquil, in which we enjoy the good things given to us in quiet and sweetness. Whoever is ungrateful to these is cursed.

units.la: Tertium, Qui mouit limitem proximi: Quo lex furti plenius explicatur. Et eodem pertinent falsæ literæ, vastationes regionum, priuilegijs spoliare subditos.
units.tr: Third, Cursed is he who removes his neighbour's landmark. By this the law against theft is more fully explained. To the same category belong false letters, the devastation of regions, and the stripping of subjects of their privileges.

units.la: Quartum, Qui cæcum errare facit. Afflictis non illudere, sed condolere & benefacere est hominis. Cæcus quia nec mundi, in quo viuit, nec quibuscum agit conspectu frui potest, miser est: eius miseriam grauare illusionibus est pesimum.
units.tr: Fourth, Cursed is he who makes the blind to wander. It is a human duty not to mock the afflicted but to sympathise with them and do them good. The blind man, since he cannot enjoy the sight of the world in which he lives or of those with whom he deals, is wretched; to aggravate his misery with deceptions is the worst thing.

units.la: Cur ergo mundum in tenebris ignorantiæ, & in vmbra mortis iacentem sunt qui suis falsis dogmatibus decipiant magis? Nihil dicunt cum dicunt: mundus vult decipi: illorum erat fallacias detegere. Peccant etiam magistratus, iudices, notarij, aduocati qui miserorum rusticorum iurgijs atq; controuersijs gaudent, & suffundunt frigidam, vt pascantur diutius. Eidem maledictioni sunt obnoxij qui stultos homines faciunt suis sannis stultiores, quique a-dolescentium mores corrumpunt.
units.tr: Why then are there those who deceive still more, with their false doctrines, a world lying in the darkness of ignorance and in the shadow of death? When they say, "The world wants to be deceived," they say nothing; it was their task to expose the deceptions. Magistrates, judges, notaries and advocates also sin, who rejoice in the quarrels and disputes of wretched peasants and pour cold water on them so that they may be fed upon longer. Those who make foolish men still more foolish with their mockery, and who corrupt the morals of young people, are liable to the same curse.

units.la: Quintum, Qui declinare facit iudicium pupilli, viduæ, peregrini, &c. Scelus, hoc est, & officio & iureiurando magistratuum contrarium: vt ne dicam charitatem & officium & naturā hominis.
units.tr: Fifth, Cursed is he who perverts the judgment of the fatherless, the widow and the stranger, etc. This is a crime contrary to the duty and oath of magistrates, not to say to charity, to duty and to human nature.

units.la: Sextum, Qui dormit cum vxore patris. Hoc anathema simul cum septimo, octauo, nono, venerem illicitam remouet, & requirit vt casti simus & sancti.
units.tr: Sixth, Cursed is he who lies with his father's wife. This curse, together with the seventh, eighth and ninth, removes forbidden lust and requires that we be chaste and holy.

units.la: Decimum, Qui proximum suum clam occidit. Puta insidijs, veneno, quocunque modo.
units.tr: Tenth, Cursed is he who secretly kills his neighbour. That is, by ambush, by poison, or by any other means.

units.la: Eodem etiam vndecimum pertinet, quo prohibetur ne quæstum ex eorum qui nos non læserunt sanguine venemur.
units.tr: The eleventh also pertains to the same matter, by which it is forbidden to hunt gain by the blood of those who have not harmed us.

units.la: His omnibus additur maledictum esse qui non his verbis omnibus steterit. Qui locus ostendit nullam esse nostram iustitiam, sed aliunde atq; ab eo quem lex & prophetæ monstrant petendam esse, testis est apostolus Gal.3.
units.tr: To all these is added that cursed is he who does not abide by all these words. This place shows that there is no righteousness in us, but that it must be sought elsewhere, and from him whom the law and the prophets point to; the apostle is a witness to this in Gal. 3.

units.la: Atq; hæc Deus ita suo populo proponi voluit atq; explicari: nempe, vt hoc externo ritu populares animos moueat, quo legem & probent & se seruaturos recipiant.
units.tr: God wished these things to be set before his people and explained in this way, namely, so that by this outward rite he might move the minds of the common people, that they might both approve the law and receive it with the intention of keeping it.

units.la: In quo cernimus Deum bonum patrem, & salutis nostrae supra quàm potest dici cupi-dum[?]: quippe qui non modo quid facto opus sit proponat atq; doceat, verum etiam ad id nos quoquo possit modo pertrahat atq; alliciat: deniq; etiam in officio retineat. Est recta vitæ ra-tio non ita difficilis cognitu, sed factu longè difficillima: pauci per arctam multi per latam viam eunt. Unde reuocentur necesse est. Sunt qui sibi peccaturis vellent angelum retrahen-tem mitti. At alijs magis efficacibus rationibus Deus vtitur: modo eas acciperemus. Adhibet enim parentes, magistros, magistratus, iudicia, poenas & praemia, nostrum ipsorum confen-sum, quò fit vt ipsi nollemus licere, quod liberet in nos alijs: dat etiam boni maliq́ue sensum & cognitionem, quibus voluntates percellantur.
units.tr: In this we see God as a good Father, and one who cares for our salvation beyond what can be said. For he not only sets forth and teaches what must be done, but also draws and entices us to it in every possible way, and finally keeps us in our duty. The right rule of life is not so hard to know, but very hard indeed to practise: few go by the narrow way, many by the broad. Those who go astray must therefore be called back. Some would wish an angel to be sent to hold back those about to sin; but God uses other, more effective means, if only we would accept them. He employs parents, teachers, magistrates, courts, punishments and rewards, and our own consent, so that we ourselves would not want to be allowed what others are free to do to us. He also gives a sense and knowledge of good and evil, by which our wills are struck.

units.la: Sed his omnibus addunt visibiles, easq; sacrosanctas actiones. Veluti cum iurant sublatis digitis: cum more Macedonum panis frangitur: cum Romano more porca feritur. Eodem modo ritum hunc sancit, vt animos hominum percellat.
units.tr: But to all these he adds visible and most sacred actions: as when they swear with raised fingers; as when, after the manner of the Macedonians, bread is broken; as when, after the Roman manner, a pig is struck. In the same way, he sanctions this rite so that it may strike the minds of men.

units.la: In quo consideranda sunt subiectum, attributum, assensus noster. Subiectum est homo, qui seruat aut transgreditur præcepta.
units.tr: In this we must consider the subject, the predicate and our assent. The subject is the man who keeps or transgresses the precepts.

units.la: Attributum est, quod ei tribuitur: seruanti, vt sit Baruch, hoc est, benedictus, laudatus, bonus, beatus: transgredienti, vt sit Arur, id est, maledictus, inglorius, malus, miser, perditus.
units.tr: The predicate is what is ascribed to him: to the one who keeps them, that he may be Baruch, that is, blessed, praised, good, happy; to the one who transgresses, that he may be Arur, that is, cursed, dishonoured, evil, wretched, lost.

units.la: Assensum huic sententiæ præbent omnes, quippe qui dicant, Amen. Etsi enim peccatum a nobis perpetratum solemus eleuare, quoad spes est euadendi: tamen cum ab alijs est patra-tum, & elabi non possumus amplius, culpam quanta quanta est confitemur.
units.tr: All give their assent to this sentence, since they all say "Amen." For although we are accustomed to lighten a sin committed by ourselves, as long as there is hope of escaping, yet when it has been committed by others, and we can no longer escape, we confess the guilt, however great it is.

units.la: Ex quo perspicuum est in quanta mala, qui legem transgreditur, sese proijciat: quantisq; rursus augeat sese bonis, qui illi feruet. Vt eâ ope Christi præditi[?] seruemus faxit deus, Amen.
units.tr: From this it is plain into how many evils he throws himself who transgresses the law, and with how many goods he again enriches himself who keeps it. May God grant that, endowed with that help of Christ, we keep it, Amen.

units.la: CAPVT XXVIII. SERMO LXVIII.
units.tr: Chapter 28. Sermon 68.

units.la: SI diligenter audieris vocem Domini Dei tui, & custodieris, fecerisq; omnia præcepta mea, quæ ego præcipio tibi hodie, ponet te Dominus Deus tuus excelsiorem cunctis nationibus terræ.
units.tr: If you diligently hearken unto the voice of the LORD thy God, to observe and to do all his commandments which I command thee this day, the LORD thy God will set thee on high above all the nations of the earth.

units.la: 2 Venientq; super te omnes benedictiones istæ, & apprehendent te, si audieris vocem Domini Dei tui.
units.tr: And all these blessings shall come on thee, and overtake thee, if thou shalt hearken unto the voice of the LORD thy God.

units.la: 3 Benedictus eris in vrbe, benedictus in agro.
units.tr: Blessed shalt thou be in the city, and blessed shalt thou be in the field.

units.la: 4 Benedictus fructus ventris tui, fructus telluris tuæ, atq; fœtus iumentorum tuorum, fœtus boum tuorum & gregum ouium tuarum.
units.tr: Blessed shall be the fruit of thy body, and the fruit of thy ground, and the fruit of thy cattle, the increase of thy kine, and the flocks of thy sheep.

units.la: 5 Benedicta sporta[?] tua, atq; reliquiæ tuæ.
units.tr: Blessed shall be thy basket and thy store.

units.la: 6 Benedictus eris cum ingredieris, benedictus cum exieris.
units.tr: Blessed shalt thou be when thou comest in, and blessed shalt thou be when thou goest out.

units.la: 7 Efficiet Dominus vt hostes tui, qui aduersum te insurgunt, ante te corruant: Per iter vnum egredientur aduersum te, & per septem vias fugient ante faciem tuam.
units.tr: The LORD shall cause thine enemies that rise up against thee to be smitten before thy face: they shall come out against thee one way, and flee before thee seven ways.

units.la: 8 Mandabit Dominus, vt super te (veniat) benedictio in promptuaria tua, atque in omnia ad quæ admolitus fueris manum tuam, fortunabitq; te in terra, quam Dominus Deus tuus dat tibi.
units.tr: The LORD shall command the blessing upon thee in thy storehouses, and in all that thou settest thine hand unto; and he shall bless thee in the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee.

units.la: 9 Eriget te Dominus sibi in populum sanctum, sicut iurauit tibi, si mandata Dei tui custodieris, & in vijs eius incesseris.
units.tr: The LORD shall establish thee an holy people unto himself, as he hath sworn unto thee, if thou shalt keep the commandments of the LORD thy God, and walk in his ways.

units.la: 10 Omnes populi terræ videbunt, quod nomen Domini inuocatum sit super te, & timebunt à te.
units.tr: And all people of the earth shall see that thou art called by the name of the LORD; and they shall be afraid of thee.

units.la: 11 Dominus quoq; te reliquum faciet, idq; bono (tuo) in fructu ventris tui, in fœtu iumentorum tuorum, & in proventu telluris tuæ, in terra, quam iurauit Dominus patribus tuis, vt daret (eam) tibi.
units.tr: And the LORD shall make thee plenteous in goods, in the fruit of thy body, and in the increase of thy cattle, and in the fruit of thy ground, in the land which the LORD sware unto thy fathers to give thee.

units.la: 12 Aperiet tibi Dominus thesaurum suum bonum, nempe cœlum, vt det pluuiam terræ tuæ suo tempore, & vt benedicat vniuerso operi manus tuæ, vt possis mutuo dare gentibus multis, tu verò nihil mutuo accipias.
units.tr: The LORD shall open unto thee his good treasure, the heaven, to give the rain unto thy land in his season, and to bless all the work of thine hand: and thou shalt lend unto many nations, and thou shalt not borrow.

units.la: 13 Ponet quoq; te Dominus in caput, & non in caudam, eriscq; duntaxat supra, nec vnquam eris infra: si audieris præcepta Domini Dei tui, quæ ego præcipio tibi hodie, vt custodias & facias.
units.tr: And the LORD shall make thee the head, and not the tail; and thou shalt be above only, and thou shalt not be beneath; if thou hearken unto the commandments of the LORD thy God, which I command thee this day, to observe and to do them.

units.la: 14 Ne deflectas à cunctis sermonibus, quos ego præcipio vobis hodie, neq; ad de-xteram neq; ad sinistram, vt eas post deos alios, & eos colas.
units.tr: And thou shalt not turn aside from any of the words which I command thee this day, to the right hand, or to the left, to go after other gods to serve them.

units.la: VPERIORE Cap. Moses externum quendam ritum introduxit, quo fideles eo propelleret, ut verbum diuinum & approbarent, & ad eius se studium obligarent. Quod quidem ad pietatis & probitatis studia multum momenti potest afferre. Quod enim ceu bonum & omnibus recipiendum approbaris, quo ore postea re-probabis? quod te seruare velle bona fide recepisti, id irritum habere nequaquam potes. Quò fit ut obligationis conscientia ad faciendum officium vehementer impellat: minimeq; mala sunt hinc deducta argumenta: ut fœdere coniunctus es, iuratus es, conductus es: ergo opem feres, promissa facies, nauabis operam. Eodem modo Moses argumentatur: legem diuinam ut iustam, bonam, æquam, utilem approbasti, teq; seruare velle recepisti: igitur seruabis.
units.tr: In the previous chapter Moses introduced a certain outward rite, by which he would drive the faithful to approve the divine word and to bind themselves to its pursuit. This indeed can contribute much weight to the pursuit of piety and uprightness. For what you have approved as good and to be received by all, with what mouth will you afterwards reject? What you have received with good faith, that you desire to keep, you can by no means hold void. Hence the consciousness of obligation powerfully urges you to perform your duty; and not unfitting arguments are drawn from this: you are bound by covenant, you have sworn, you have been hired; therefore you will bring aid, you will fulfil your promises, you will do your work. In the same way Moses argues: you have approved the divine law as just, good, equitable and useful, and you have accepted that you wish to keep it; therefore you will keep it.

units.la: Sed commodi nostri studio tantopere ducimur, ut etsi quid nos facere deceat, atq; æquum fit norimus bene: tamen aliunde spe lucri melioris affulgente, iusto & decoro quod utile fit anteponamus, minimeq; quod officij fit nostri faciamus. Qua de causa nonnunquam & in Deum & in homines iniurij sumus: sunt q; maioris apud nos ponderis quæ ex utilitate, quam quæ ex officio ducuntur argumenta.
units.tr: But we are so led by regard for our own advantage that, even if we know well what is fitting for us to do and what is right, nevertheless, when some hope of greater gain shines from elsewhere, we put what is useful before what is just and proper, and we do not do what is part of our duty. For this reason we sometimes do wrong both to God and to men; and arguments drawn from advantage carry more weight with us than those drawn from duty.

units.la: Igitur adductis atq; explicatis ijs, quæ ex officio sumpserat, argumentis, iam illa ab utili deducta addit, eaque contrariorum expositione vehementer exaggerat. Eiusmodi enim est hoc caput, ut quantopere expediat verbo Dei studere: quo loco benedictiones refert: contra quàm malum sit ea violare: quo loco maledictiones habet: intelligamus. Unde & duabus partibus constat: quarum altera benedictiones, altera maledictiones commemorat.
units.tr: Therefore, having adduced and explained the arguments taken from duty, he now adds those drawn from advantage, and he strongly amplifies them by setting out the contraries. For this chapter is of such a kind that we may understand how greatly it is profitable to be zealous for the word of God, where he recounts the blessings, and, on the other hand, how evil it is to violate it, where he has the curses. Hence it also consists of two parts, one of which recalls the blessings, the other the curses.

units.la: Utilis est utrinq; doctrina. Etenim boni, officij sui: sui amantes, utilitatis: improbi, malorum vitandorum studio ad seruanda præcepta Dei propellentur. In quo bonorum & malorum origo atque causa cernitur.
units.tr: The teaching is useful on both sides. For the good are moved by a sense of their duty, those who love themselves by a sense of their advantage, and the wicked, in their eagerness to avoid evils, are driven to keep the precepts of God. In this the origin and cause of good and evil men is seen.

units.la: Sed in præsentia de benedictionibus, seu bonis: ubi de causis primum, deinde bonis ipsis disseritur.
units.tr: But for the present the discussion concerns the blessings, or goods: where first the causes are treated, then the goods themselves.

units.la: De bonorum causa ad hunc modum : Si diligenter audieris vocem Domini Dei tui, & custodieris fecerisq;[?] omnia præcepta mea, quæ ego præcipio tibi hodie, ponet te dominus Deus tuus ex-celsiorem cunctis nationibus terræ, venientq;[?] super te benedictiones illæ omnes, &c. Quibus verbis ostendit felicitatem ex diuini verbi studio prorsus omnem proficisci. Præclarum profecto & salutare dogma quod passim approbant sacræ literæ.
units.tr: Concerning the cause of the good, it runs in this manner: If thou diligently hearken unto the voice of the LORD thy God, and observe and do all his commandments which I command thee this day, the LORD thy God will set thee on high above all the nations of the earth; and all these blessings shall come upon thee, etc. By these words he shows that all happiness arises entirely from zeal for the divine word. This is truly an excellent and salutary doctrine, which the sacred letters approve everywhere.

units.la: Sed ne quis in hoc errore ingruat: ac vel in vero Dei verbo versemur perperam, vel pro Dei verbo falsa quædam amplectamur hominum placita: Moses hæc exacte quæq; qualiaq; sint definit. Verbum ipsum appellat, vocem domini Dei tui: tum vocat, præcepta per ipsum iam tradita: quorum altero originem, altero substantiam verbi diuini monstrat.
units.tr: But lest anyone fall into this error, either that we are mistaken in the true word of God, or that we embrace certain falsehoods of men as if they were the word of God, Moses defines exactly what these things are and of what kind. He calls it the word itself, the voice of the LORD thy God; then he calls them the commandments already delivered through it; in the one he shows the origin, in the other the substance of the divine word.

units.la: Origo verbi Deus est, cuius voce & verbis est præditum: nec ex Ægypto, Italia, Græcia, sed cœlitus allata philosophia. Pater cœlestis sua voce patriarchis & prophetis eam explicauit, Hebr.1. Et unigenitus Dei filius, qui est in sinu patris enarrauit nobis, Ioan.1. Et Spiritus sanctus prophetas afflauit, 2.Pet.1. Idem habes de Dei sapientia, 1.Cor.1. scriptum. Facessant ergo humana placita qualiacunq; sint ac videantur: omnes audiant vocem Dei.
units.tr: The origin of the word is God, by whose voice and words it is endowed: it is not a philosophy brought from Egypt, Italy or Greece, but sent down from heaven. The heavenly Father explained it by his voice to the patriarchs and prophets, Heb. 1. And the only-begotten Son of God, who is in the bosom of the Father, has declared it to us, John 1. And the Holy Spirit breathed on the prophets, 2 Pet. 1. You have the same written of the wisdom of God, 1 Cor. 1. Let therefore human opinions, of whatever kind and however they may appear, cease; let all hear the voice of God.

units.la: Verum diuini verbi substantia; ipsa quoq; est consideranda, ne pro diuinis humana recipiantur: dicit, quæ ego præcipio tibi hodie. Ex quo colligimus illud esse verbi diuini loco habendum quod Mosis, prophetarum, euangelistarum, apostolorum, aliisq; canonicis libris est comprehensum. Et quemadmodum Paulus ait, si quis aliud ab hoc diuersum angelus etiam cœlitus se afferre dixerit, non erit accipiendum.
units.tr: But the substance of the divine word must also be considered, lest human things be received in place of divine: he says, which I command thee this day. From this we gather that to be held in the place of the divine word is what is contained in the books of Moses, the prophets, the evangelists, the apostles, and the other canonical books. And as Paul says, if anyone should say that an angel from heaven brings something else different from this, it is not to be received.

units.la: Iam etiam in hoc non parum situm est, ut bono tanto recte utamur. Velut enim errat ac peccat qui pro vero falsum amplectitur: sic errat & peccat magis qui veritate, qua potitus est, abutitur. Diligenter igitur hoc addit Moses, ut audiamus, faciamus, custodiamus. Quo & ple-nam rei cognitionem atq; facultatem, & actionem etiam ipsam postulat. Contemplatio requirit diligentem meditationem & inquisitionem rei. Unde dicit Dominus Ioan. 6. Scrutamini scripturas. Quo videntur auditio, lectio, meditatio verbi Dei pertinere.
units.tr: Moreover, in this too lies no small matter, that we use so great a good rightly. For just as he errs and sins who embraces what is false in place of what is true, so he errs and sins more who abuses the truth he has obtained. Therefore Moses adds this carefully: that we may hear, do, and observe. By this he requires both full knowledge and ability of the matter, and action too. Contemplation requires diligent meditation and inquiry into the matter. Hence the Lord says in John 6: Search the Scriptures. By this, hearing, reading and meditating on the word of God seem to be included.

units.la: Actio vero hoc postulat, ut ad cognitam diuinæ voluntatis normam totus homo quan-tus quantus est, animo & corpore & rerum externarum possessione reformetur atq; compo-natur: ut nihil à verbo Dei diuersum cogitet, loquatur, faciat. Id enim ni fiat verbi diuini co-gnitio non solum eum non beat, verum etiam damnat. Seruus enim sciens & non faciens vo-luntatem plagis multis afficietur: vir audiens & non faciens voluntatem Domini super are-nam domum suam ponit: populus vitam à Dei præceptis alienam agens videtur ore & labijs potius quàm corde Deum venerari: qui Abrahæ filij volunt esse eos Abrahami opera præsta-re necesse re necesse est: qui volunt arbores bonae dici, eos fructus bonos ferre decet: qui fidem suam nolent videri mortuam, vivae fidei fructus edent.
units.tr: Action, however, requires this: that by the norm of the divine will known, the whole man, whatever he is, be reformed and arranged in soul and body and in the possession of external things, so that he thinks, speaks and does nothing different from the word of God. For if this is not done, the knowledge of the divine word not only does not make him blessed, but even condemns him. For the servant who knows and does not do the will is beaten with many stripes; the man who hears and does not do the will of the Lord builds his house upon sand; a people living a life alien to God's precepts seems to honour God with mouth and lips rather than with heart; those who wish to be sons of Abraham must perform the works of Abraham; those who wish to be called good trees must bear good fruit; those who do not wish their faith to be seen as dead must produce the fruits of living faith.

units.la: Ergo simul haec ambo coniuncta sint necesse est, verbum Dei purū putum & verum, & eius ipsius in omni vitae genere studium assiduū. Hinc enim bonorū possessio proficiscitur.
units.tr: Therefore these two things must be joined together: the word of God, pure, simple and true, and constant zeal for it in every kind of life. For from this the possession of good things proceeds.

units.la: Vnde etiam dicit: Ponet te Dominus Deus tuus excelsiorem cunctis, &c. Magni boni in loco est excellere videlicet aliquarum virtutum nomine. Id verbi divini studio comparari Moses hic dicit.
units.tr: Hence he also says: "The Lord your God will set you above all, etc." To excel above others, namely in the name of some virtues, is a great good. Moses here says that this is obtained by zeal for the divine word.

units.la: Dein, Omnes benedictiones apprehendent te, inquit: nam verbo barach omne felicitatis genus & fauoris, & emolumenti quod quis alij praestiterit comprehendit. Sic felices & fortunati fuere Nohe, Abraham, Ioseph, Dauid, Machabaei, Constantinus, alij. Et populus Israel antiquitate, rebus gestis, terra, imperio, sapientia, potentia clarissimus fuit. Deus illos semper adiuvit, nec illis vnquam, nisi deficientibus, defuit.
units.tr: Then he says, "All blessings shall come upon you": for the Hebrew word barach embraces every kind of happiness and favour, and every advantage that one person bestows on another. So Noah, Abraham, Joseph, David, the Maccabees, Constantine and others were happy and fortunate. And the people of Israel was most renowned for antiquity, deeds, land, empire, wisdom and power. God always helped them, and never failed them, except when they were failing.

units.la: Et certe si vel vniversam Heluetiam, vel hanc eius metropolim Tigurum, quantum opibus, authoritate, sapientia, gloria creuerit: quanto fit ornatior omni cultu jam inde ab eo tẽ-pore, quo Christum suscepit, aestimes, Mosem vel ex eo ipso verum dicere comperies. Vrbs enim ipsa structuris sic est restaurata, ut iis qui hic olim fuere, pene tota nova nunc appareat: Senatus prudentibus, eloquentibus, fortibus viris refertus est: schola abundat doctissimis & celeberrimis viris: populus abundat claris artificibus: aerarium auctum est decimis, censibus, vectigalibus: respub. praefecturis atq; arcibus creuit. Nec quicquam est quod aegros, egenos, miseros reddat quàm crapula, luxus, nostra ipsorum scelera: & quam vita ad Dei verbum cō-posita gloriam assequimur, eam remissione disciplinae omnem amittimus.
units.tr: And surely, if you consider how much Switzerland as a whole, or its metropolis Zurich, has grown in resources, authority, wisdom and glory, and how much more adorned it has become with every kind of refinement since the time it embraced Christ, you will find that Moses speaks the truth even from this fact alone. For the city itself has been so rebuilt that it now appears almost entirely new to those who once lived here. The Senate is full of prudent, eloquent and brave men; the school abounds in most learned and renowned men; the people abound in distinguished craftsmen; the treasury has been enlarged by tithes, taxes and tolls; the commonwealth has grown in prefectures and fortresses. Nor is there anything that makes men sick, needy and wretched so much as gluttony, luxury and our own wickedness; and by relaxing discipline we lose entirely the glory that we gain by a life ordered according to the word of God.

units.la: Bona verò, quoniâ ei non cum doctis solùm & sapientibus viris, sed etiam cum vulgo ho[?] minimum est oratio: non qua solent eruditi serie, sed ordine vulgari recitat: primum immobilia quae nos ligendo, id est, iacentia: tum mobilia quae nos farendo, hoc est, vaga seu mobilia vocamus: denique rerum quas privatim atq; publicè gerimus successus refert.
units.tr: Now, since he speaks not only with learned and wise men but also with the common people, his speech is not arranged in the manner that scholars usually follow, but in the ordinary order: first the immovable goods, which we call those that lie fixed, that is, the lands; then the movable goods, which we call those that move, that is, wandering or movable things; and finally he relates the successes of the things we manage both privately and publicly.

units.la: De bonis immobilibus dicit: Faustus erit in urbe & in agro. Quae requiruntur ad vrbis felicem statum, ut cives ad belli pacisq; negocia aptos atq; idoneos: ut iuris & aequitatis ob-servatione, ut religione recta: denique eius finem felicitate, quae est in animi, corporis, fortunae bonis habeat. Ut situs sit salubris, opportunus, tutus; ut vrbs habeat artes & negociationes.
units.tr: Of immovable goods he says: "You shall be blessed in the city and blessed in the field." What is required for the happy state of a city is that its citizens be fit and suited for the affairs of war and peace; that it be governed by the observance of law and equity, and by true religion; and finally that its end be happiness, which lies in the goods of the mind, the body and fortune. That its site be healthful, convenient and safe; that the city have arts and trade.

units.la: De mobilibus dicit, fructu ventris, id est erunt liberi felices & boni. Ingens Dei munus est habere liberos, maius habere sanos & vegeto corpore: maximū habere eosdē frugi et obsequentes. Fructum telluris, ut vinum, frumentum & reliqua. His & pecus addit, in quo si succedat negotiatio plurimum est lucri. Negotiorum successus, hoc ipso fore felices dicit, quod ingressum & egressum faustum pollicetur. His addit victoriam, annonam, & alia: postremo authoritatem & existimationem.
units.tr: Of movable goods he says, "the fruit of your body," that is, your children will be happy and good. It is a great gift of God to have children, a greater one to have them healthy and vigorous in body, and greatest of all to have them thrifty and obedient. "The fruit of your land, such as wine, grain and the rest." To these he adds livestock, in which, if trade succeeds, there is much profit. He says that the successes of their undertakings will make them happy in this very thing, that he promises "a blessed going out and coming in." To these he adds "victory, abundance of food, and other things"; lastly, "authority and reputation."

units.la: Haec bona quaerunt homines: sed hominum fauore & auxilio potius quàm divina gratia Moses eorum authorem Deum monstrat & illius ope comparari posse. Igitur ab illo solo pe-deamus in Christo Iesu. Amen.
units.tr: These are the goods that men seek; yet Moses shows God, rather than the favour and help of men, to be their author, and that they can be obtained by his aid. Therefore let us beg for them from him alone in Christ Jesus. Amen.

units.la: SERMO LXIX.
units.tr: SERMON LXIX.

units.la: 15 Quod si vocem Domini Dei tui non audieris, ut custodias & facias cuncta praecepta eius, & statuta eius, quae ego praecipio tibi hodie, venient super te omnes execrationes istae, & apprehendent te.
units.tr: 15 But if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the LORD thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee.

units.la: 16 Execratus eris tu in urbe, execratus in agro.
units.tr: 16 Cursed shalt thou be in the city, and cursed shalt thou be in the field.

units.la: 17 Execrata erit sporta tua, & reliquiae tuae.
units.tr: 17 Cursed shall be thy basket and thy store.

units.la: 18 Execratus fructus ventris tui, & fructus telluris tuae, foetus boum tuorum, & greges ouium tuarum.
units.tr: 18 Cursed shall be the fruit of thy body, and the fruit of thy land, the increase of thy kine, and the flocks of thy sheep.

units.la: 19 Execratus in introitu tuo, execratus in exitu tuo.
units.tr: 19 Cursed shalt thou be when thou comest in, and cursed shalt thou be when thou goest out.

units.la: 20 Mittet Dominus in te egestatem, conturbationem & increpationem, in omnia quae instituerit, & quae fecerit, donec deleat te, & perdat te subitò, propter malitiam studiorum tuorum, quibus me deseruisti.
units.tr: 20 The LORD shall send upon thee cursing, vexation, and rebuke, in all that thou settest thine hand unto, until thou be destroyed, and until thou perish quickly, because of the wickedness of thy doings, whereby thou hast forsaken me.

units.la: 21 Adhaerescere faciet tibi Dominus pestem, donec consumat te de superficie terrae, in quam tu venis ut eam possideas.
units.tr: 21 The LORD shall make the pestilence cleave unto thee, until he have consumed thee from off the land, whither thou goest to possess it.

units.la: 22 Percutiet te Dominus tumore, ardore, & inflammatione, aestu consumente, siccitate, robigine, aurigine, & insequentur te donec pereas.
units.tr: 22 The LORD shall smite thee with a consumption, and with a fever, and with an inflammation, and with an extreme burning, and with the sword, and with blasting, and with mildew; and they shall pursue thee until thou perish.

units.la: 23 Erunt tibi coeli super caput tuum aereï[?], & tellus quae sub te est ferrea.
units.tr: 23 And thy heaven that is over thy head shall be brass, and the earth that is under thee shall be iron.

units.la: 24 Dabit Dominus terræ tuæ pro pluuia arenam & puluerem, de cœlis descendet super te, donec fueris deletus.
units.tr: 24 The LORD shall make the rain of thy land powder and dust: from heaven shall it come down upon thee, until thou be destroyed.

units.la: 25 Dabit quoq; te Dominus prostratum ante hostes tuos, ad quos vno itinere egredieris, & per septem itinera coram eis fugies, eritq; vt caput (super te) commoueas omnia regna terræ.
units.tr: 25 The LORD shall cause thee to be smitten before thine enemies: thou shalt go out one way against them, and flee seven ways before them; and thou shalt be tossed among all the kingdoms of the earth.

units.la: 26 Erit præterea cadauer tuum cibus omni volucri cœli, & bestiæ terræ, nec erit qui absterreat.
units.tr: 26 And thy carcase shall be meat unto all the fowls of the air, and unto the beasts of the earth, and no man shall frighten them away.

units.la: 27 Percutiet quoq; te Dominus vlcere Ægyptiaco, ficu, scabie fluida & scabie sicca, ita vt sanari non possis.
units.tr: 27 The LORD will smite thee with the botch of Egypt, and with the emerods, and with the scab, and with the itch, whereof thou canst not be healed.

units.la: 28 Percutiet te Dominus amentia, cæcitate & subita conturbatione cordis.
units.tr: 28 The LORD shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart.

units.la: 29 Et eris palpans in meridie, quemadmodum palpat cæcus in tenebris, neque prospereris in viis tuis: & omnino talis eris, qui vim & iniuriam patiatur, quiq; diripiatur: idq; cunctis diebus, nec erit qui eripere possit.
units.tr: 29 And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways: and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee.

units.la: 30 Vxorem tibi desponsabis, & alius cum ea concumbet: domum extrues, & nō habitabis in ea: vineam quoq; plantabis, & non prophanabis eam.
units.tr: 30 Thou shalt betroth a wife, and another man shall lie with her: thou shalt build an house, and thou shalt not dwell therein: thou shalt plant a vineyard, and shalt not gather the grapes thereof.

units.la: 31 Bos tuus mactabitur spectantibus id oculis tuis, & tu non comedes ex eo: asinus tuus rapietur à conspectu tuo, nec reuertetur ad te. Oues tuæ tradentur hostibus tuis, nec erit qui tibi auxilium ferat.
units.tr: 31 Thine ox shall be slain before thine eyes, and thou shalt not eat thereof: thine ass shall be violently taken away from before thy face, and shall not be restored to thee: thy sheep shall be given unto thine enemies, and thou shalt have none to rescue them.

units.la: 32 Filij tui & filiæ tuæ tradentur populo alij, & oculi tui spectantes hoc tabescent super his tota die, nec erit tantum virium vt sis ferendo.
units.tr: 32 Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people, and thine eyes shall look, and fail with longing for them all the day long: and there shall be no might in thine hand.

units.la: 33 Fructum terræ tuæ, & vniuersum laborem tuum comedet populus quem tu non nouisti: eritq; omnino talis qui vim et iniuriam patiatur, ac conquassetur omnibus diebus.
units.tr: 33 The fruit of thy land, and all thy labour, shall a nation which thou knowest not eat up; and thou shalt be only oppressed and crushed alway.

units.la: 34 Vasanus quoq; eris propter ea quæ oculis tuis videre cogeris.
units.tr: 34 So that thou shalt be mad for the sight of thine eyes which thou shalt see.

units.la: 35 Percutiet te Dominus vlcere noxio in genubus & cruribus, quod curari nequaquam poterit, à planta pedis tui vsq; in verticem tuum.
units.tr: 35 The LORD shall smite thee in the knees, and in the legs, with a sore botch that cannot be healed, from the sole of thy foot unto the top of thy head.

units.la: 36 Ducet te Dominus, regemq; tuum, quem constituisti super te, ad gentem, quam nec tu nouisti, nec patres tui, & seruies illic dijs alijs, nempe lapidi & ligno.
units.tr: 36 The LORD shall bring thee, and thy king which thou shalt set over thee, unto a nation which neither thou nor thy fathers have known; and there shalt thou serve other gods, wood and stone.

units.la: 37 Eris, vt à te stupeant, te exemplo vtantur, de te linguam acuant omnes populi ad quos te Dominus duxerit.
units.tr: 37 And thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all the nations whither the LORD shall lead thee.

units.la: 38 Multum seminus[?] proferes in agrum, parum colliges, vastabit illud locusta.
units.tr: 38 Thou shalt carry much seed out into the field, and shalt gather but little in; for the locust shall consume it.

units.la: 39 Vineas plantabis & coles, sed vinum non bibes, neq; colliges, eò quod vermis sit illud absumpturus.
units.tr: 39 Thou shalt plant vineyards and dress them, but shalt neither drink of the wine, nor gather the grapes; for the worms shall eat them.

units.la: 40 Olea erunt tibi per cunctos fines tuos, & tamen non vnges te oleo, quia excutietur olea tua.
units.tr: 40 Thou shalt have olive trees throughout all thy coasts, but thou shalt not anoint thyself with the oil; for thine olive shall cast its fruit.

units.la: 41 Filios & filias generabis, & nullos habebis: quia abibunt in captiuitatem.
units.tr: 41 Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but thou shalt not enjoy them; for they shall go into captivity.

units.la: 42 Omnes arbores tuas, & fructus terræ tuæ perdet arugo.
units.tr: 42 All thy trees and the fruit of thy land shall the blight consume.

units.la: 43 Peregrinus qui tecum habitat, ascendet & te sublimior erit, & tu longè infra desidebis.
units.tr: 43 The stranger that is within thee shall get up above thee very high; and thou shalt come down very low.

units.la: 44 Ipse tibi mutuo dabit, & tu illi nihil dabis mutuo: ipse erit in caput, & tu eris in candam.
units.tr: 44 He shall lend to thee, and thou shalt not lend to him: he shall be the head, and thou shalt be the tail.

units.la: CVm omnes homines sic natura sint comparati, vt sui ipsorum honoris, commodi, voluptatis sint auidi, optimeq; ea sequi possint ac velint: contra sui dedecoris, damni, exitij horrore concutiantur: ac propterea alia re nulla perinde ac promissione boni, & commonitione mali quascunq; ad res propelli possint: sanè Deus pro suo summo ac singulari nos conseruandi studio passim bona promittit ijs qui ipsum audiant ac sequantur, & rursus mala rebellibus comminatur. Nam neq; bona propterea pollicetur, vt quam reipsa declarat verbis etiam nobis attestetur gratiam, neq; mala minatur ideo vt suam nobis ostentet omnipotentiam: verum vt ad bonum adducat bona pollicetur, vt absterreat à malis minitatur mala. Atq; id quidem cogitandum est etiam in hoc 28.cap. Quo benedictiones bonis, maledictiones malis indicantur:nempe Deum non ideo bona promittere vt humana more bonitatem & beneficentiam suam iactitet:quis enim hunc mundum & quae in eo sunt intuens, atq; etiam immensa in nos beneficia Dei recolens id nescit? nec mala minitari, quo terribilem sese faciat, ac ceu homo superbus sui metum imbellibus incutiat: quis enim grauiter punita scelera & iustitiam eius aestimans id non senserit?
