The heavenly Father, good and provident, gave him to the upright, that is, to believers. The goods we have in him are victory over Satan, tranquillity of conscience, food suited to both bodies and souls, and wholesome souls too. We ourselves are moreover a great people in Christ and, as Peter says, a royal priesthood. To Christ be honour for ever. Amen.

units.la: CAPVT XXXIIII. SERMO XIX.
units.tr: CHAPTER 34. SERMON 19.

units.la: 1 Ascendit itaq; Moses ex campis planis Moab in montem Nebo, & in ver-ticem collis, qui est è regione Ieriche, ostenditq; illi Dominus vniuersam terram Gi-lead vsq; Dan.
units.tr: 1 So Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of the hill that faces Jericho. And the LORD showed him all the land of Gilead as far as Dan,

units.la: 2 Et omnem Naphtali, & terram Ephraim atq; Manasse, & omnem terram Iuda vsq; ad mare nouissimum.
units.tr: 2 and all Naphtali, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and all the land of Judah as far as the western sea,

units.la: 3 Meridiem deniq;, & campestrem planitiem Ieriche, quæ est ciuitas palma-rum, vsq; Zor.
units.tr: 3 and the South, and the plain of the valley of Jericho, the city of palm trees, as far as Zoar.

units.la: 4 Et ait Dominus ad eum: Hæc est terra quam iuraui Abrahamo, Isaac & Iacob, & dixi semini tuo dabo eam, vt oculis tuis videres, illuc verò non introires.
units.tr: 4 And the LORD said to him: This is the land which I swore to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, saying, I will give it to your seed. I have let you see it with your eyes, but you shall not go over there.

units.la: 5 Mortuus igitur est Moses seruus Domini in terra Moab iuxta os Domini.
units.tr: 5 So Moses the servant of the LORD died there in the land of Moab, at the mouth of the LORD.

units.la: Q[?]VONIAM ad existimationem doctrinæ Dei momenti multum affert authorita-te & beneuolentia præstare eos, qui illam ipsam profitentur: sanè quo doctrina Dei per Mosem reuelata plus virium atque existimationis habeat, fit instinctu at-que impulsu Spiritus sancti, vti quinto huic Mosis libro ceu doctrinæ Mosaicæ capiti, in primisque decem Dei legum expositioni caput hoc 34. ceu encomium Mosis adij-ciatur. Atq; hoc ipsum quidem ab Iofua,prophetico spiritu scriptum fuisse Hebræi tradunt. At Philo in vita Mosis scribit eum præuisam spiritu prophetico mortem suam & populo prædixisse, & vna cum fui ipsius sepultura viuum adhuc mandaffe literis. Quod argumento foret hoc ipsum caput non minus quam librum totum ipsius authoris scriptum esse.Et est hoc ipsum impendio probabile: quando suam sibi mortem diuinitus reuelatam superiore capite pro concione dixit.Sunt autem verba Philonis hæc: Συμμαρτυρούμενον ὃ καὶ τὸ τέλος τῆς ἱε[?]ρῶν γραμμάτων, ὁ καθάπερ ἐν τῇ ζωῇ κεφαλὴ τῆς ὅλης νομοθεσίας ἔχειν. ἡδὴ δὲ ἀναλαμ[?]βανόμενος, καὶ ἐπ' αὐτῆς βαλβίδ[?]ος ἐσῳς, ἵνα τὸν εἰς ἀεὶ [?]δρόμον ... [illegible, ~12 letters] ... En ut finem sacrorum Mosis voluminum, quo summa ac caput iuris continetur, omnium maximè admirandum existimet, ecquare[?] quod eius author iam assumendus,& in ipsis stans carceribus unde in cœlum excursurus erat, diuino spiritu afflatus,viuens de se ceu mortuo prophetauit: ac priusquam mortuus esset mortuum se & sepultum esse narrauit.
units.tr: Since it contributes much to the esteem of God's teaching that those who profess it should be men of authority and goodwill, the teaching of God revealed through Moses gains more strength and esteem from this: by the prompting and impulse of the Holy Spirit, this chapter 34 has been added to this fifth book of Moses, as a kind of crown of the Mosaic teaching, and especially of the exposition of the Ten Commandments, as a eulogy of Moses. The Hebrews hand down that this very chapter was written by Joshua under prophetic spirit. But Philo, in his Life of Moses, writes that Moses, foreseeing his death by the prophetic spirit, both foretold it to the people and committed it to writing, together with his own burial, while still alive. This would be an argument that this chapter, no less than the whole book, was written by its author himself. And this is very probable indeed, since in the previous chapter he spoke to the assembly of his death, which had been revealed to him by God. Philo's words are these: [Συμμαρτυρούμενον ὃ καὶ τὸ τέλος τῆς ἱερῶν γραμμάτων, ὁ καθάπερ ἐν τῇ ζωῇ κεφαλὴ τῆς ὅλης νομοθεσίας ἔχειν.] Behold how he thought most admirable the end of the sacred books of Moses, in which the sum and head of the whole law is contained: that their author, already taken up and standing on the very starting-line from which he was to rush into heaven, inspired by the divine Spirit, prophesied of himself while living as though dead, and before he died related that he was dead and buried.

units.la: Cæterùm hoc capite primum eius mors,tum quæ sunt eam consecuta describuntur.
units.tr: Moreover, in this chapter his death is first described, and then what followed upon it.

units.la: Et ad mortis descriptionem duas circumstantias affert locum & mortem ipsam : unde perspicuum est quo loco quoq; modo sit mortuus.
units.tr: For the description of his death, it gives two circumstances: the place and the death itself. From these it is plain in what place and in what manner he died.

units.la: Ac quo loco sit mortuus hoc ipso docet quod dicit, sese ascendisse ex campestribus Moab in montem Nebo in verticem collis, &c. Est ergo locus in quo Moses obijt,Pisga vertex montis Nebo in terra Moab.
units.tr: The place where he died is shown by what it says: that he went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of the hill, and so on. The place in which Moses died is therefore Pisgah, the summit of Mount Nebo, in the land of Moab.

units.la: Quod autem saluti Mosis eo ipso nihil detrahitur, quod in terra idololatrica mortem obit:id nobis ipsis est etiam documento,ut vbi moriamur nihil referre existimemus.Vt enim omne solum forti patria est: sic quocunq; loco pium mors obruerit, ibi viam illi ad quietem sempiternam sternit.Mortui sunt in Ægypto, in deserto,in Babylone, in Assyrijs multi prisci patres:mortui sunt etiam apostoli alij alibi:nec vllum inde senserunt salutis dispendium. Sic Mosi in terra Moabitica mori nil nocuisse Christi prophetarum,apostolorum, Dei patris ipsius testimonia significant.
units.tr: That Moses' salvation loses nothing because he died in a land of idolaters should also be a lesson for us, that we should count it of no importance where we die. For as every soil is a home to the brave, so wherever death overtakes a godly person, there it prepares his way to eternal rest. Many of the ancient fathers died in Egypt, in the wilderness, in Babylon and among the Assyrians; other apostles died elsewhere, and they suffered no loss of salvation from it. So the testimonies of Christ, of the prophets, of the apostles, and of God the Father himself signify that it did no harm to Moses to die in the land of Moab.

units.la: At inquis,patres in terra Canaan sepeliri voluere : verum hoc est inquam : sed id factum ab eis est ad confirmandam posteris fiduciam eius potiundi. Vt mors ipsa non nocet,sic nec locus in quo morimur obest credentibus. Peregrini cum simus in hoc mundo,non est cogitandum quod nuspiam expediat mori,quàm ibi vbi natus fis.
units.tr: But you will say that the fathers wished to be buried in the land of Canaan. That is true, I answer, but they did it to confirm in their posterity the confidence of obtaining it. As death itself does not harm, so neither does the place where we die harm believers. Since we are strangers in this world, we need not think it matters where we die rather than where we were born.

units.la: Iam quod videt etiam terram promissam:& eius quæ cis Iordanem est , partem iam ipse distribuerat:id exemplo est firmas esse & certas Dei promissiones. Veluti quę promisit Ada-mo,Abrahamo,Dauidi,toti priscæ ecclesiæ,ea præstitit omnia.
units.tr: Now, that he sees the promised land, and that he had already assigned the part of it on this side of the Jordan, is an example that God's promises are firm and sure. Whatever he promised to Adam, Abraham, David and the whole ancient Church, he has fulfilled in every respect.

units.la: Quod denique iam iam moriturò refricatur peccati memoria:idq; ab eo qui quid nobis expediat explorate cognitum habet : id nobis est indicio vt mortis sic peccati recordatio-nem esse salutarem.Ergo vt in omni vita mortis:sic in morte peccatorum meminisse & pœni tentia duci, & apud Christum veniam quærere prodest. At sunt qui conscientiam placent ac sopiant,velintq; nec mortis nec peccatorum mentionem sibi fieri:nempe securi vt sint & dolore nullo turbentur. Deus contra Mosem & mortis admonet & peccati,eoq́ue ipso minimè malè consulit.
units.tr: Finally, that the memory of sin is stirred up in him just as he is about to die, and that by him who knows for certain what is good for us, is a sign to us that the remembrance of sin is as salutary as the remembrance of death. Therefore, as in all of life we should remember death, so in dying it is profitable to remember our sins, to be brought to repentance, and to seek pardon from Christ. But there are some who would soothe and lull their conscience, and wish that neither death nor sins be mentioned to them, namely so that they may be secure and not troubled by any grief. God, on the contrary, reminds Moses both of death and of sin, and in this he by no means counsels badly.

units.la: Verum hic est etiam typus quidam.Vt enim Moses videt & monstrat terram promissam: in eam ipsam autem nequaquam introduci:sic lex videt qua via ad Deum fit eundum,sed eò nos nequaquam perducit. Quare lege ceu pædagogo ad Christum euntes vtimur : illo vero potiti ad beatæ vitæ possessionem peruenie mus.
units.tr: But here there is also a certain type. For as Moses sees and points out the promised land, yet is by no means brought into it, so the law sees by what way we must go to God, but by no means leads us to him. Therefore, going to Christ as to a schoolmaster, we use the law; but when we have obtained him, we arrive at the possession of the blessed life.

units.la: Quomodo mortuus sit paucis expressit verbis : Mortuus est igitur Moses seruus Domini, &c. In quo profecto quæ sit hominum differentia & iusta inter se comparatio cernitur. Magnus est alius sapientia,alius robore,potentia: alius opibus & honoribus:quisquis sis eundem habebis cum ignobili atque obscura plebe communem finem. Quam fortes Samson & Dauid? quàm prudens Solomon? quàm formosus Absolom? quàm potens Nabuchodono-zor? quàm diues Nabal? & tamen omnes sunt mortui. Quid interest inter eorum qui mortui sunt cadauera? nulla sunt quibus secernantur aurea,argentea,serica ornamenta. Quid igitur efferimur? quid alius alium contemnimus?
units.tr: How he died is expressed in a few words: So Moses the servant of the LORD died, and so on. In this indeed is seen the difference between men and their just comparison with one another. One man is great in wisdom, another in strength and power, another in wealth and honours; whoever you are, you will share the same end with the ignoble and obscure common people. How strong were Samson and David? How wise was Solomon? How handsome was Absalom? How mighty was Nebuchadnezzar? How rich was Nabal? And yet all are dead. What difference is there among corpses of those who have died? There are none by which the golden, silver and silken ornaments are distinguished. Why then are we lifted up? Why do we despise one another?

units.la: Sed obijcis: ergo nullum virtutis erit studium, nullum item pietatis & fidei. Esto maxi-mum. Etsi enim mors eosdem omnes faciat: tamen id fit quoad ipsam, non autem quoad eos qui moriuntur. Multum enim interest inter latronem qui dixit, si veneris in regnum tuum memor esto mei Domine: & inter eum qui dixerat, si filius Dei es, fac ut & nos & tu ipse de cruce descendamus. Mortui sunt extra terræ promissæ limites non tam exploratores decem quàm Moses & Aharon, sed tamen multum inter eos interest. Mortui sunt & Achab & quos ipse est persecutus prophetæ: sed multum interest. Comparavit humana fors Christo Barra-bam, imò prætulit: sed longè est alia eorum ratio. Moriuntur in acie cum qui pro pecunia, tum qui pro patria belligerantur: sed magna est eorum status differentia.
units.tr: But you object: then there will be no zeal for virtue, none for godliness and faith. Granted, to the greatest extent. For although death makes them all alike, yet this happens as far as death itself is concerned, not as far as those who die are concerned. For there is a great difference between the thief who said, Lord, remember me when you come into your kingdom, and him who had said, If you are the Son of God, make both us and yourself come down from the cross. Those who died outside the limits of the promised land were not so much the ten spies as Moses and Aaron, yet there is a great difference between them. Both Ahab and those whom the prophet himself persecuted died, yet there is a great difference. Human chance compared Barabbas with Christ, indeed preferred him; yet their case is far different. Some fight and die in battle for money, others for their country; yet the condition of these is very different.

units.la: Intelligendum est igitur non minorem mortis quàm vitæ anteactæ differentiam esse: ac qui hic voluere esse Domini potius, quàm huius mundi fideles asseclæ [?], ij procul ab ijs qui cum mundo condemnati sunt remoti in cœlo cum Christo sempiternis gaudijs perfruen-tur, Amen.
units.tr: We must understand, therefore, that there is no less difference between death and the life that went before it. Those who here chose to be the Lord's rather than faithful followers of this world will be set apart far from those who are condemned together with the world, and in heaven with Christ they will enjoy eternal joys, Amen.

units.la: SERMO XX.
units.tr: SERMON XX.

units.la: 6 Et sepeliuit eum in valle in terra Moab contra domum Peor, & nullus hominum cognouit sepulchrum eius in hunc usq; diem.
units.tr: 6 And he buried him in a valley in the land of Moab, over against the house of Peor; but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day.

units.la: 7 Erat autem Moses natus centum & viginti annos quum moreretur, oculi eius non caligarant, maxillæ eius nihil defecerant.
units.tr: 7 And Moses was an hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated.

units.la: 8 Defleruntq; filij Israel Mosen in planitie campestri Moab triginta diebus, & completi sunt dies fletus & luctus Mosis.
units.tr: 8 And the children of Israel wept for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days: so the days of weeping and mourning for Moses were ended.

units.la: 9 Iehosua verò filius Nun repletus est spiritu sapientiæ, eò quod posuerit Moses manus suas super eum, obedieruntq; filij Israel ei, & fecerunt sicut præceperat Dominus Mosi.
units.tr: 9 And Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him: and the children of Israel hearkened unto him, and did as the LORD commanded Moses.

units.la: 10 Et non surrexit Propheta amplius in Israele sicut Moses, quem nosset Dominus facie ad faciem.
units.tr: 10 And there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face.

units.la: 11 Secundum omnia signa & prodigia propter quæ miserat eum Dominus, ut faceret in terra Ægypti coram Pharaone & omnibus seruis eius atq; coram universa terra eius.
units.tr: 11 In all the signs and the wonders, which the LORD sent him to do in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh, and to all his servants, and to all his land.

units.la: 12 Et secundum cunctam manum robustam, & omnem terrorem magnum, quæ fecit Moses in oculis totius Israelis.
units.tr: 12 And in all that mighty hand, and in all the great terror, which Moses wrought in the sight of all Israel.

units.la: CVm in huius ultimi Cap. principio sit auditum quo loco, quoque modo magnus ille Moses vitæ suæ finem fecerit: iam quasi quædam doctrinæ vitæq; eius conclusio proponitur: qua cognoscamus quænam eius mortem consecuta sint. Ac primum quidem quomodo sepultus sit: dein ut Iosue ei in officio successerit: postremò quàm sui nominis memoriam post se reliquerit monstratur.
units.tr: Since at the beginning of this last chapter it has been heard where and how that great Moses brought his life to an end, now, as it were, a certain conclusion of his teaching and life is set forth, by which we may learn what followed his death: first, how he was buried; then, that Joshua succeeded him in office; lastly, it is shown how he left behind the memory of his name.

units.la: Ac de sepultura quidem pauca, sed diligenter omnia dicit: ut de persona sepeliente, de loco quo sepultus sit, de eo qui sepultus sit, de luctu populi.
units.tr: Of his burial indeed he says little, but he tells everything carefully: concerning the person who buried him, the place where he was buried, the one who was buried, and the mourning of the people.

units.la: De sepeliente: & sepeliuit eum. Sic enim habent & Hebraea veritas & Chaldaica paraphrasis. At LXX. interpretes habent, ἔταφαν [?] sepelierunt: quasi illum filij Israel sepelierint. Quod ideo falsum esse necesse est, quia sepulchrum eius à nemine est unquam cognitum. Qui enim aliquis hominum sepelijsset eum, & sepulchrum illius non esset cognitum? Quare fieri potest ut scriptum sit ἔταφαν [?] pro ἔταφεν [?], quod facillimè fieri potuit. Quare creditur ab ip-so Deo vel eius angelis sepultus esse.
units.tr: Concerning the one burying: and he buried him. For thus the Hebrew truth and the Chaldee paraphrase have it. But the Seventy translators have [ἔθαψαν], "they buried," as though the children of Israel had buried him. This must be false, because his sepulchre was never known to anyone. For what man would have buried him and yet not have known his sepulchre? Therefore it can be that [ἔθαψαν] was written for [ἔθαψεν], which could very easily happen. Hence it is believed that he was buried by God himself or by his angels.

units.la: Quod igitur tantus vir è conspectu cœtuque hominum sublatus est, & sepultus, ut nemo hominum ubinam sepulchrum eius esset unquam cognorit: ac Iudas apostolus scripserit diabolum operam dediße, ut sepulchrum eius proderet hominibus, sed impeditum esse ab angelis: Id argumento est, homines quando vita functi fuerint non ullis arcis concludendos, sed humandos esse. Dicit enim Dominus: Cinis es & in cinerem reuerteris. Sepulti sunt etiam patriarchæ: à suis discipulis Iohannes Baptista, à viris religiosis Stephanus: ipseque Christus licet in cœlum ascensurus esset, tamen prius voluit sepeliri. Valeant igitur cum suis reliquijs papistæ: disputet & iurgetur cum Vigilantio quoad vel-lit Hieronymus; tamen maior Dei Mosem sepelientis nobis erit authoritas. Neq; enim abie-cta sacrarum literarum authoritate, quod eum Iosephus scribit euanuisse in quadam specu, cum nubes repente eum obtexisset, recipimus: quando opinione eadem spreta Philo qui & ipse Iudæus fuit sacras literas secutus eum mortuum, [illegible, ~12 letters] sepultum esse docet.
units.tr: That such a great man was taken from the sight and company of men and buried, so that no one ever knew where his sepulchre was; and that the apostle Jude wrote that the devil made an effort to betray his sepulchre to men, but was hindered by the angels: this is evidence that when men have died they are to be buried, not shut up in any chests. For the Lord says: "Dust thou art, and unto dust thou shalt return." The patriarchs too were buried; John the Baptist was buried by his disciples, Stephen by pious men; and Christ himself, although he was about to ascend into heaven, nevertheless wished first to be buried. Let the Papists, then, keep their relics with themselves; let Jerome dispute and wrangle with Vigilantius as much as he likes; still, the authority of God burying Moses will be greater for us. For we do not accept, having cast aside the authority of Holy Scripture, what Josephus writes, that he vanished in a certain cave when a cloud suddenly covered him; since Philo, who was himself a Jew and followed the sacred writings, rejects that opinion and teaches that he, having died, [illegible] was buried.

units.la: Cæterum quòd Iudas apostolus ex Apocryphis refert Michaelem archangelum de Mo-sis corpore cum diabolo decertasse, id Oecumenius in epistolam Iudæ sic exponit: [illegible, ~40 letters] (inquit) [illegible, ~60 letters] [illegible, ~50 letters] dem de re in libris [illegible, ~8 letters] Origenes, & in 3. cap. epistolæ ad Titum scribens Hieronymus. Quæ cum non sint institutæ scriptionis omittimus: ac simpliciter credimus quod Mosem Dei seruum mortuum & sepulchro conditum sacræ literæ prædicant.
units.tr: As for the fact that the apostle Jude, out of the Apocrypha, reports that the archangel Michael contended with the devil over the body of Moses, Oecumenius explains this in his commentary on the Epistle of Jude as follows: [illegible] (he says) [illegible] [illegible]. On this matter in the books [illegible] Origen, and Jerome writing on chapter 3 of the Epistle to Titus. Since these things do not belong to the purpose of our writing, we omit them, and we simply believe what the sacred writings proclaim, that Moses, the servant of God, died and was laid in a sepulchre.

units.la: Locus dicitur vallis oppositadomui seu phano Peor. Eius exemplo disce quòcunque loco sepeliare non magnopere laborandum. Interea loca sepeliendis mortuis destinata nolumus turpiter haberi: aut homines mortuos nihilo, quàm pecora, reuerentius condi: sed superstitionem & desperationem abesse. Referatur huc locus Diui Pauli in 1. Thess. 4. principio. Multi laborant de loco quo condi velint, sed vbi sepelitur ille sanctissimus? quo visum est Domino: hominibus omnibus incognito videlicet sepulchro.
units.tr: The place is called the valley opposite the house or temple of Peor. From his example learn that one should not labour greatly over the place where one is buried. Meanwhile we do not wish the places set aside for burying the dead to be treated shamefully, nor dead men to be laid in the ground with less reverence than cattle; but superstition and despair are to be absent. Let the passage of the divine Paul in 1 Thessalonians 4 at the beginning be referred here. Many labour over the place where they wish to be laid; but where is that most holy man buried? Where it pleased the Lord: the sepulchre being unknown to all men, of course.

units.la: Iam & persona quæ sepelitur est inspicienda. Dicit annos natum 120. Longum profecto vitæ spacium, quodq; ei fit laudi maximæ. Sed illud magis mirandum tamen, quod dicitur tanta senectus ei nullum incommodum attulisse: quodq; adhuc & oculorum acie valuerit, & facies ei fuerit suculenta ac viuida.
units.tr: Now also the person who is buried must be considered. It says he was 120 years old. Truly a long span of life, and one that is a very great praise to him. But it is still more to be wondered at that it says such great old age brought him no discomfort, and that his eyesight was still strong and his face was still full of juice and vigour.

units.la: In quo nobis sunt proposita præclara vitæ documenta duo. Vnum, quod pij probiq; & sapientes homines, quoniam vitam & pie & temperanter agunt suam, longæui sint & sani & firmi. Nam cum senescant ob innatum calorem corpora sintq; longæui maximè, qui maximè sunt humidi, vt Galenus perhibet: minimè mirum est eos suam sibi vitam ipsos minuere, qui vino, Venere, balneis, crapula cum exiccant atque inflammant corpora, tum vitiosis humori-bus replent. Eodem pertinet etiam quod ambitio, auaritia, inuidia multi sibi tabem accer-sunt seq; ipsi miserè exedunt. Quibus malis atque miserijs quoniam pij vel vacant vel saltem imperant: fieri potest facile, vita hac terrena, vt fruantur & suauiore & diuturniore.
units.tr: In this we have set before us two outstanding lessons of life. The first is that pious, upright and wise men, since they conduct their life both piously and temperately, are long-lived, sound and robust. For although bodies grow old through their innate heat, and those are most long-lived which are most moist, as Galen reports, it is least surprising that those who shorten their own life are those who dry out and inflame their bodies with wine, Venus, baths and gluttony, and then fill them with vicious humours. To the same point belongs the fact that many, through ambition, avarice and envy, bring corruption upon themselves and miserably consume themselves. Since the pious either are free from these evils or at least rule over them, it can easily happen that they enjoy this earthly life more pleasantly and for longer.

units.la: Testantur hoc omnium populorum atque etiam hominum exempla, quæ descripta sunt omnibus historijs, ea secula videlicet quibus esset frugalitas & temperata victus ratio, longe-uos homines tulisse. Refert enim Plinius accidisse Romæ, vt vnum quinquennium euoluere-tur quo nullus senator moreretur. Nec infitias eo nonnullos esse, qui victus acurata ratione longæuitatem multum iuuent suam: veluti Pollionem Romulum centesimum annum excé-dentem Augustus Cæsar hospes fertur interrogasse, qua nam ratione vigorem illum animi corporisq; custodisset, rursum accepisse: intus mulso, foris oleo. Memorandum est etiam no-stratis illius rustici responsum, qui cum nonaginta circiter annos natus vegeto firmoq; esset adhuc corpore, valeretq; etiam animi bonis, rogatus quo pacto suæ valetudini consuluisset, vti adeo multos in annos vitam prorogasset, fertur respondisse: se tametsi impigrè semper laborasset, tamen à mensa nunquam resurrexisse adeo saturum, quin illi plus ciborum ca-pere libuisset: indicans se quàm parcissimè corpus curasse atque ab omni crapula abstinui-se. Mirandum est etiam aliquos in vrbe viros longæuos adhuc valere: quod temperantia sunt assecuti. At nostra ætate necesse est multos præmatura morte auferri, quod luxu crapulaque sese eant perditum. Moses autem quia pius fuit & temperans ideo multos in annos vixit.
units.tr: The examples of all peoples and even of men, which are recorded in all histories, bear witness to this: namely, that those ages in which there was frugality and a temperate manner of living produced long-lived men. For Pliny reports that it happened at Rome that a five-year period passed in which no senator died. Nor do I deny that there are some who, by a carefully regulated diet, greatly help their own longevity: for example, it is said that Augustus Caesar, as a guest, asked Pollio, a Roman who had passed his hundredth year, by what method he had preserved that vigour of mind and body, and received the answer: honeyed wine within, oil without. It is also worth recalling the answer of that rustic of our own land, who, being about ninety years old, still vigorous and firm in body, and possessed of good mental powers as well, was asked how he had cared for his health, and how he had prolonged his life for so many years. He is said to have replied that, although he had always worked diligently, he had never risen from the table so full that he did not still want to take more food; thereby indicating that he had cared for his body as sparingly as possible and had abstained from every excess. It is also to be wondered at that some elderly men in the city are still healthy, because they have attained this by temperance. But in our age it is necessary that many are carried off by early death, because they have ruined themselves by luxury and gluttony. Moses, however, because he was pious and temperate, therefore lived for many years.

units.la: Alterum est quod hinc discimus, quod etiam in maximis molestijs & miserijs vitaque asperrima Deus possit suos saluos atque incolumes conseruare. Veluti in illis defertis locis, per quæ populum suum exÆgypto traduxit, eorū vestes atque calceos ne atterentur confer-uauit: in Babylone Danielis socios ijs qui regios cibos comederunt, pinguiores fecit. Quam obrem ne labores detrectes & pericula fretus auxilij diuini spe & fiducia.
units.tr: Another lesson we learn from this is that God can keep his people safe and unharmed even amid the greatest troubles and the harshest hardships. Thus in those barren places through which he led his people out of Egypt, he kept their clothes and shoes from wearing out; in Babylon he made the companions of Daniel, who ate the king's food, fatter than the others. Therefore do not shrink from labours and dangers, but rely on the hope and confidence of divine help.

units.la: De luctu populi dicit, Deflerunt eum Israelitæ triginta diebus. Quo exemplo discimus quæ moderatè fiunt circa sepulturam non reprehendi: modum enim præscribit apostolus pro-
units.tr: Concerning the mourning of the people he says, "The Israelites mourned for him thirty days." From this example we learn that those things which are done moderately around burial are not to be found fault with. For the apostle prescribes the measure of such grief, on account of the hope of the resurrection.

units.la: [illegible, ~6 letters] pter spem resurrectionis. Nolite contristari de dormientibus sicut gentes quæ spem non habent resurrectionis. Ac quoniam qui hinc ad superos commigrarunt in meliorem vitam sunt ingressi: non est eis quicquid sunt assecuti fœlicitatis inuidendum.
units.tr: …[illegible] on account of the hope of resurrection. "Do not grieve for those who sleep, as the Gentiles do, who have no hope of resurrection" (1 Thess. 4). And since those who have departed hence to the heavenly ones have entered into a better life, the happiness they have attained is not to be envied them.

units.la: Quomodo Iosue successerit. Iosua vero, inquit, filius Nun repletus est spiritu sapientiæ eo quod posuerit Moses manus, &c. Quibus verbis docet ipsum Iosuam, quoniam a Domino per Mosem ad remp. gubernandam electus esset, etiam spiritu sancto donatum esse, ita ut non solum ipse facultatem scientiamque rerum gerendarum haberet: sed etiam populus obedientiam ei debitam præstaret.
units.tr: How Joshua succeeded. "Now Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom, because Moses had laid his hands upon him," etc. In these words he teaches that Joshua himself, since he had been chosen by the Lord through Moses to govern the commonwealth, was also endowed with the Holy Spirit, so that he not only had the ability and knowledge to conduct affairs, but the people also rendered him the obedience due to him.

units.la: Et ea de re tria dicit. 1. Repletum spiritu sapientiæ: quod documento est & magistratibus ad officium suum obeundum opus esse sapientia, & id donum ijs potisimum diuinitus dari, qui legitimè & diuinitus eliguntur. Nam cum populus sit bellua multorum capitum, & quot sunt capita totidem sint, vt fertur prouerbio, quoq; sensus: omnibus ijs regendis quis nisi sapientissimus sufficeret? Agnorunt hoc prisci reges, qui plæriq; sapientiæ studuerunt: vt Melchisedek rex & sacerdos: vt Ægyptij reges plæriq; etiam philosophi: vt Dauid & Solomon: vt aliarum gentium reges atque principes literarum atque philosophiæ studio clari. Alexan-der Macedo, Mithridates Ponti rex, Augustus, Iulius, Cicero: vt Romani Cæs. summa do-ctrina atque sapientia præditos homines secum habuere. At hæc iam studia plæriq; magistratus & principes despiciunt. Vnde & existunt innumeræ calamitates.
units.tr: On this matter he says three things. (1) "Full of the spirit of wisdom": which is a lesson that magistrates need wisdom to discharge their office, and that this gift is given by God chiefly to those who are lawfully and divinely chosen. For since the people is a beast of many heads, and there are as many opinions as there are heads, as the proverb goes, who would be equal to governing all of them unless he were most wise? The ancient kings recognised this, most of whom devoted themselves to wisdom: such as Melchizedek, king and priest; such as the kings of Egypt, most of whom were also philosophers; such as David and Solomon; such as the kings and princes of other nations, renowned for their devotion to letters and philosophy. Alexander of Macedon, Mithridates king of Pontus, Augustus, Julius, Cicero: and the Roman Caesars kept about them men endowed with the highest learning and wisdom. But now most magistrates and princes despise these studies. Hence innumerable calamities arise.

units.la: Cæterum idem exemplum, vt dictum est, docet Deum ei quem eo vocarit donis ad id necessarijs instruere: vt Iosephum, Mosem, Samsonem, Danielem, hic Iosuam bonis ad negocia sua necessarijs instruxit.
units.tr: Moreover, as has been said, the same example shows that God equips with the gifts necessary for the task the one whom he has called to it: as Joseph, Moses, Samson, Daniel; here he furnished Joshua with the gifts necessary for his affairs.

units.la: Sed & causa redditur hoc loco. Quia posuerat Moses manus eius super eum: hoc est, Moses iussu Dei ritè eum vocauerat, ac Deum, qui spiritu suo sancto eum imbueret, precatus elegerat. Nam impositio manuum & electionis huius & gratiæ diuinitus collatæ quasi tessera quædam est. Gen. 48. Iacob benedicturus Ephraim & Manasse capitibus eorum manus imponit. Et 1. Tim. 4. Ne neglexeris quod in te est donum, delegatum tibi ad prophetandum, idq; roboratum est manuum impositione à senioribus. Circa hanc fiebant preces. Vnde Augustinus li. 3. de baptismo contra Donat. cap. 16. Quid enim, inquit, aliud est manuum impositio quàm oratio super hominem?
units.tr: But a cause is also given in this place: "Because Moses had laid his hands upon him": that is, Moses, at God's command, had duly called him, and having prayed to God, who would imbue him with his Holy Spirit, had chosen him. For the imposition of hands is a kind of token both of this election and of the grace conferred by God. Gen. 48: Jacob, about to bless Ephraim and Manasseh, lays his hands on their heads. And 1 Tim. 4: "Neglect not the gift that is in you, given to you for prophesying, which was confirmed by the imposition of hands of the elders." Prayers were made around this rite. Hence Augustine, book 3 on baptism against the Donatists, chapter 16: "For what else," he says, "is the imposition of hands than prayer over a man?"

units.la: Ex quo colligimus in electione magistratuum religiosè riteq; versandum esse: quid enim boni sperandum sit inde, si in ipso rei principio peccatum sit?
units.tr: From this we gather that in the choice of magistrates one must act religiously and duly: for what good can be hoped from it, if sin was committed at the very beginning of the matter?

units.la: Deinceps addit, Obedieruntq; ei, &c. En vnde obedientia. Si magistratus plenus sit spiritu sapientiæ, religiosè riteq; electus, tunc sperari potest tranquillum pacatumq; imperium. Quis enim stultiori, malis artibus ad rerum summam euecto, & improbo obediat? At admiratione virtutum tracti homines ducuntur & reguntur facillimè.
units.tr: Next he adds, "And the children of Israel obeyed him," etc. Behold whence obedience comes. If the magistrate is full of the spirit of wisdom and has been chosen religiously and duly, then a tranquil and peaceful rule can be hoped for. For who would obey a foolish man, raised to the height of power by wicked arts, and a wicked one? But men are drawn and governed most easily by admiration for virtues.

units.la: Iam Mosis mortem ea fama secuta est, non ortum post vnquam illius similem principem. Ea laus si spectes ipsum qui laudatur Mosem, docebit eniti vt famam nobis mortuis optimam relinquamus: eaq; de re magis quam de opibus soliciti simus.
units.tr: Now after Moses' death that reputation followed him, that no prince like him arose afterwards. If you look at this praise in Moses himself who is praised, it teaches us to strive to leave behind an excellent reputation when we are dead, and to be concerned about this rather than about riches.

units.la: Si nos consideres, indicio fuerit quanti sanam doctrinam faciamus, quam diuinitus accepta Moses tradidit. Præuidit spiritus sanctus fore qui illum explosum vellent: sed aliud extat hoc loco testimonium. Quomodo enim vel aduersus Turcam vel Iudæos fidei nostræ veritatem tuebimur, si quos ipse sibi Christus testes asciuit Mosem, prophetas, psalmos, respuamus? Quamobrem cum spiritus sanctus hanc ei deferat laudem: ipsum quidem vt diuiuitus orbi datum doctorem reuerebimur: doctrina autem eius ceu Dei verbum amplectemur. Quo fiet vt in eo viuamus, per Iesum Christum Dominū nostrum, Amen.
units.tr: If you consider us, it will be a sign of how highly we value sound doctrine, which Moses handed down, having received it from God. The Holy Spirit foresaw that there would be those who wished to reject it; but this passage offers yet another testimony. For how shall we defend the truth of our faith against the Turk or the Jews, if we reject Moses, the prophets and the Psalms, whom Christ himself adopted as his witnesses? Wherefore, since the Holy Spirit bestows this praise on him, we shall revere him indeed as a teacher given to the world by God, and we shall embrace his doctrine as the word of God. By this we shall come to live in it, through Jesus Christ our Lord, Amen.

units.la: FINIS.
units.tr: THE END.
